0.content:
Aisa Bathhouse (also: Aisa Sentou, Sea Duck Bathhouse): The Aisa Bathhouse is an indoor bathhouse in Inazuma City's Tenryou district, inspired by the volcanic hot springs of Natlan. It offers a spa, fine dining and, since a renovation led by Yumemizuki Mizuki, psychotherapy from yumekui-baku (dream-eating) psychologists. Samurai of the Tenryou Commission are among its regulars.

Aikawa Susumu opened it after visiting Natlan and manages it day to day; Mizuki, the major shareholder, directs its important decisions. Many Inazumans treat it as a go-to place to relax. The bathhouse's map text mentions rumours of a special investor behind the scenes.

Geography: In Tenryou, within Inazuma City. It has a hot-spring hall and a therapy room; the signboard shows a sea-duck and reads "ST" in the Inazuman script, probably an abbreviation of the Japanese sentou (public bath). The Japanese name 秋沙銭湯 uses "aisa", a kind of sea duck.

People: Aikawa Susumu is the owner, called "Boss" by neighbours but says Mizuki is the real boss. Two baku staff, Hyakujitsuhaku Shion and Shiba Murasaki, appear after the quest Dream Eater's Melancholia. Yumemizuki Mizuki is the clinical psychologist and major shareholder, and a yumekui-baku who devours nightmares to ease patients.

Culture: The bathhouse sells "warmth for body and soul" in a Natlan-inspired setting. Aikawa says the spring water has restorative power, and reports that guests, including Tenryou samurai, speak candidly while bathing.

History: Aikawa went to Natlan, fell in love with the hot springs there and, once home, wanted friends in Inazuma to feel the same, but had no funds. Mizuki, then living among the People of the Springs, heard of the plan and invested a large sum, becoming the core founding investor. After the events of Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (Natlan), she returned to Inazuma and renovated the bathhouse, adding therapy sessions to wide acclaim.

Quests: Dream Eater's Melancholia (Mizuki's story quest, Tapirus Somniator Chapter, 5.4): the Traveler is invited to the bathhouse with a VIP pass after meeting Mizuki, receives therapy, and helps look into the rival clinic.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Aisa Bathhouse is open and popular. It has operated since Inazuma opened (2.0), was renovated after Natlan, and Mizuki is working on expanding the brand.

1.comment: Aisa Bathhouse: Yumemizuki Mizuki and the Therapy Service
1.content: Yumemizuki Mizuki is a renowned clinical psychologist and a yumekui-baku, a dream-eating yokai. She eats a patient's nightmares and works through the emotions that come with them, which is a heavy burden for her. She runs one-on-one sessions at the bathhouse and sits behind its important decisions. The Traveler once finds her crying at the shore, where she explains this is the final stage of digesting the nightmares, when she feels all of their negative emotions.

2.content:
Amakane Island (also: Amakane-jima, Sweet Gold Island): Amakane Island is a small festival island just off the western coast of Byakko Plain on Narukami Island, Inazuma. Its name means roughly "Sweet Gold Island". In the in-game description, people sit among its blooming sakura in summer to watch fireworks in the distance.

It is a gentle, recreational spot rather than a settlement: a few vendors and Yashiro Commission representatives are stationed there. Canon says very little else about it, so treat it as a scenic viewing place.

Geography: The island lies a short way off the west coast of Byakko Plain. From its shore one can look across the water at Inazuma City, whose fireworks are visible from here.

People: Four open-world NPCs are placed on the island: Hirohiko and Takami, both Yashiro Commission representatives; Murakami, a street food vendor; and Sanden, a vendor. The wiki gives no further background for them.

Culture: The in-game description, credited to Cissie in the Version 2.0 Special Program, pictures a summer scene: people seated beneath blossoming sakura, watching fireworks far off. The island is called a festival island, which fits the food vendors and the Yashiro Commission presence.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Amakane Island is unchanged: a quiet festival spot in Inazuma.

3.content:
Amakumo Peak (also: Amakumo-touge): Amakumo Peak is the fragmented, storm-wrapped heart of Seirai Island in Inazuma, a place of constant Electro tempests. Long ago the huge Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir was killed over the island and her fury was held down by wards kept at the Asase Shrine. About 500 years ago the shrine's head priestess Asase Hibiki broke those wards, and the Thunderbird's lingering regret came back as the Thunder Manifestation, which still haunts the summit.

The Traveler reaches the summit in the world quest series Seirai Stormchasers, resealing four Warding Stones to calm the storm and defeating the Thunder Manifestation, and takes away a strange feather, the Peculiar Pinion, that later matters on Tsurumi Island.

Geography: The summit is broken into fragments of stone ringed by storm cloud and is unlocked as part of Seirai Stormchasers, Part IV. At the foot of the peak lies a lake of electrified water patrolled by Ruin Sentinels, with a light-up tile puzzle on its shore. Sea Ganoderma, Onikabuto, Naku Weed and Amakumo Fruit are local specialties.

Places: The Summit: the shattered crown of the mountain, home of the Thunder Manifestation. The Lake: electrified water that must be drained to be crossed safely. The Underground Ruins: a sunken settlement of passages and gates beneath the lake, revealed once the water is gone.

History: In the lore told by the Asase Shrine and Inazuma's weapon and artifact texts, the Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir was a monster once revered on Tsurumi Island. Killed over Seirai Island by the Raiden Shogun (Ei), her leftover hatred and regret were suppressed by wards that the Asase Shrine maintained. Around 500 years ago, during the Seirai Rebellion, Asase Hibiki used what she had learned from the tengu to unseal them in support of Ako Domeki's crew against the Shogunate. The released power raised a vast Electro storm in the middle of the island and called up the Thunder Manifestation.

Dangers: Strong Electro storms and electrified water, Ruin Sentinels around the lake, hilichurls, Mitachurls, Treasure Hoarders, Nobushi and Kairagi, and above all the Thunder Manifestation on the summit.

Travel: The island has Electro Seelie and an Electro Elemental Monument; the summit and its boss open up with Seirai Stormchasers.

Quests: Seirai Stormchasers (Parts I-IV, 2.1) is the world quest series set here. The Traveler, with the Adventurers' Guild members Etsuko and Taisuke, learns about the Warding Stones from Neko, the talking cat who calls herself the Asase Shrine's provisional head priestess, seals all four stones and defeats the Thunder Manifestation.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the peak remains the stormy centre of Seirai Island; no later canon read for this entry changes it.

The Thunder Manifestation can still be fought there; the storm has been calmed by the sealed Warding Stones.

4.comment: Amakumo Peak: Thunder Manifestation and Kanna Kapatcir
4.content: Kanna Kapatcir ("Great Eagle of the Storm"), the Thunderbird, was a huge, violet-feathered bird of prey regarded as a divine guardian by the tribe of Tsurumi Island, though she paid them little attention until a boy named Ruu sang to her. His sacrifice by his own tribe drove her to destroy the mountain and everyone on it; she was later hunted down and killed by the Raiden Shogun. The Thunder Manifestation is the coagulated regret of that death, a lightning-wielding elemental being.

5.content:
Amenoma Smithy (also: Amenoma Kaji-ya, Amenoma Art): The Amenoma Smithy sits at the eastern end of Inazuma City, in Hanamizaka. Its master, Amenoma Tougo, and apprentice Hajime follow the Amenoma Art, one of the five bladesmithing schools of the Raiden Gokaden. The school is known for avoiding special tricks and relying on endless practice and willpower.

Tougo accepts only commissions for fine Jade Steel swords and knives because of his age, and sends everyday forging to Hajime. Kaedehara Kazuha says that of the old Gokaden schools only the Amenoma Clan's art survives.

Places: An ordinary craft shop with a forge and a board for orders, in Hanamizaka. The signboard reads "KJ" in Inazuman script, probably short for kaji (smithing). Hajime forges certain items and sells low-grade weapons (gameplay shop; stock matches blacksmiths elsewhere); Tougo stands in front of the building.

People: Amenoma Tougo is the master and owner; his nephew is named Amenoma Yuuya (mentioned in Kazuha's story quest). Hajime is his senior disciple, practises forging daily, earns a modest salary, and is unsure he will be the heir. Both keep repeating the phrase about patience and willpower that moves mountains.

Culture: The Amenoma Art tries to copy water, which turns stone to sand by patience. Tougo says there is nothing mystical in it, only daily practice until every motion becomes part of the smith's life. In the Raiden Gokaden tradition, a ronin is said to have taught forging to five disciples, each of whom developed a different school.

History: Around five hundred years ago, after Iwakura Michihiro beat Teruyo in a duel and founded the Iwakura Clan, he had the Amenoma master of the time forge a blade to pass to each holder of the "-in" title: the Hakuen Michimitsu Amenoma. It disappeared after Iwakura Mitsunari's death in the quest Iwakura Art's Downfall, and was later found rusted in Enkanomiya. The Amenoma Kageuchi is a second copy, given to the Saimon Clan and later to the Traveler.

Quests: Through the Mist, a Name Unveiled (Kazuha's story quest, A Strange and Friendless Road, Acer Palmatum Chapter), in which Kazuha and the Traveler ask Tougo for information. During the permanent Tatara Tales world quests, the board announces that Jade Steel supplies have temporarily stopped, so exquisite orders are paused.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the smithy continues to operate in Hanamizaka, with Tougo as owner and Hajime as apprentice. Nothing newer has been found.

6.comment: Amenoma Smithy: Amenoma Art and the Raiden Gokaden
6.content: The Raiden Gokaden are Inazuma's five bladesmithing schools; the Amenoma Art is one. It is said to have no secret tricks, only the patience and willpower to give everything. Tougo says only a few visitors have the perseverance to carry the spirit of the art.

7.content:
Araumi: Araumi is a promontory at the northern tip of Narukami Island in Inazuma, cut off from the rest of the island by Mt. Yougou to its south. Beneath it lie the ruins of an ancient city that runs down under the earth and the sea and was abandoned after the Cataclysm. Its sealed passages hide Electro puzzles, Ruin Sentinels and the sunken mansion of the tengu Reizenbou.

The upper ground holds Thunder Sakura roots and Electro puzzles; the way underground opens only through the Memento Lens, which the Traveler receives in the world quest Sacrificial Offering. Much of Araumi is underwater, and the flooded lower levels lead to the Perpetual Mechanical Array, a giant Ruin Sentinel automaton, and to the domain Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates.

Geography: A rocky northern headland of Narukami Island with a Teleport Waypoint, a Waverider Waypoint, Sakura Bloom trees and a small island group to its north-east. The ancient city is not a ruin on the surface but a stack of underground levels: wells and stairwells descend through drowned halls and passages where cube-shaped mechanisms control the water level, down to a large cavern with a wrecked ship.

Places: Notable spots: the Earth Kitsune Statue cave on the western shore; the well with three kitsune statues that opens the way down; the tower ruins at the surface; the cavern of the shipwreck; the arena of the Perpetual Mechanical Array; and the Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates, a tengu annex dwelling now sunk beneath the sea.

People: Nobody lives in Araumi now. Echoes of past inhabitants are heard only through Earth Kitsune Statues and the Memento Lens. The one living figure met underground is Acting Instructor Mifune Satoshi, an Iwakura Art practitioner hiding from the Shogunate, who fights as a Kairagi.

History: The city extended underground at the north of Narukami Island and is probably from the Archon War era, judging by its architecture. It stayed active for centuries until the Cataclysm, when its inhabitants fled; the Kitsune Saiguu is said to have led people through its underground passages to safety. The survivors never came back, and Araumi was left empty.

Dangers: Ruin Guards, Ruin Scouts and Defenders; Kairagi Mifune Satoshi; the Perpetual Mechanical Array, whose attacks include rockets, orbital strikes and cube-form charges; and Ochimusha, the defilement that appears during the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual.

Travel: Araumi can be reached by the Waverider and Teleport Waypoints on Narukami Island's northern coast. Its underground passages are sealed until the Memento Lens is used on kitsune statues in a well. The Perpetual Mechanical Array can also be reached through a portal on Jinren Island.

Quests: Sacrificial Offering (2.0) gives the Memento Lens. Cleansing Defilement (2.0) includes a ritual at Araumi, one of five places where a Thunder Sakura barrier must be broken; its final fight is against Ochimusha. Both belong to the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual series. Araumi's underground also holds Old Stone Slates and a Torn Page from Toki Alley Tales (Prologue).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Araumi is abandoned, with no residents and no reported change since its release.

The Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual at Araumi has been completed in the story. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content revisits the site.

key: Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates
8.comment: Araumi: Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates
8.content: The Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates is a tengu annex dwelling that floats on the sea like a lonely boat, deep under Araumi. It was the final abode of a tengu warrior who had abandoned the world, and was once linked with the "Yougou Three". The domain lets the Traveler solve its riddle and fight trespassing bandits: the Kairagi Dancing Thunder, joined by Fiery Might at half health. To unlock it, step on glowing panels to open the gates.

9.content: A large Ruin Sentinel automaton and world boss that guards the lowest level of Araumi's ruins. It changes between forms, such as a rocket, a rolling cube, a sword and a spinning blade, and sends out cubes that become smaller Ruin Sentinels. It drops the Perpetual Heart.

10.comment: Araumi: Memento Lens and Earth Kitsune Statues
10.content: The Memento Lens, a gadget gained in Sacrificial Offering, reveals hidden mechanisms and echoes of the past at Earth Kitsune Statues. At Araumi it unlocks the sealed passages and shows a moment from the Shogunate era, a commissioner's wish for a port, and other voices from earlier times, including a mother-and-sons exchange tied to Mikoshi Nagamasa and Iwakura Michihiro.

11.content:
Asase Shrine (also: Asase Jinja): The Asase Shrine is a subarea of Seirai Island in Inazuma. It was founded to manage the wards that hold down the lingering resentment of the Thunderbird, Kanna Kapatcir, felled over the island. The shrine is now looked after by Neko, a big black cat who calls herself its Provisional Head Priestess, waiting for the shrine maiden Asase Hibiki, who never came back from a great thunderstorm.

Around five hundred years ago, Hibiki unsealed the wards to help the pirate captain Ako Domeki against the Shogunate, which unleashed the Electro storm that still marked the island in the Traveler's time. The shrine itself was little damaged, only emptied of visitors.

Geography: A shrine on Seirai Island, in noticeably better condition and with fairer weather than the rest of the island. Features: a Rock Pile, a Waverider Waypoint, an offering box, and statues of Neko added after quests. Villagers of Koseki Village once helped upkeep it and left offerings.

Places: The offering box, which Neko has the Traveler repair so that Mora can be left in it. A statue of Neko, which Neko has Ooshima Junpei make; its finishing touch is followed by a cloud forming the shape of a cat. Renovation work and cat care also take place at the shrine. that formed the shape of a cat.

People: Neko, a black cat larger than ordinary cats, speaks to the Traveler and is the self-styled head. After the quests, the adventurers Etsuko and Taisuke (Adventurers' Guild) and Ooshima Junpei can also be found there. The shrine cats named Konbumaru (after Takamine the Mistsplitter), Hachihou and Meshi have names of "good things" passed down through generations.

History: After the Thunderbird was killed by the Electro Archon at Amakumo Peak, the shrine, managed by the Asase Clan, was established to suppress what was left of her. Hibiki trained at the Grand Narukami Shrine, mentored by the Kitsune Saiguu, and returned to Asase Shrine after the cataclysm. When Domeki's crew fought the Shogunate she broke the wards using "true magic" from the Yougou Tengu, loosing the Thunder Manifestation on the Shogun's ships. The island was devastated and Koseki Village was evacuated to Inazuma City; Hibiki disappeared into the storm.

Quests: Seirai Stormchasers (Parts I-IV, a world quest series after Ritou Escape Plan): the Traveler meets Neko, repairs the offering box, seals four Warding Stones with Etsuko and Taisuke, and faces the Thunder Manifestation. The separate Neko Is a Cat series has Neko has the Traveler renovate the shrine and tend the cats, and takes a trip to the Grand Narukami Shrine.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine stands renovated, with Neko still waiting for Hibiki's return. Sealing the Warding Stones quieted the island's storm.

12.comment: Asase Shrine: Neko, Provisional Head Priestess
12.content: Neko is a large black cat who can speak to people and says human ears cannot usually understand cats. She addresses the Traveler grandly, refers to herself as Her Ladyship, and sets them tasks. She expects Hibiki to return and is ready to introduce the Traveler and friends to her. She remains unaware that the village has been empty for hundreds of years. When she visits the Grand Narukami Shrine she is amazed by its offering box but insists her own shrine is better.

13.content:
Autake Plains (also: Autake Heigen, Plains of Autake): Autake Plains is a subarea of Tsurumi Island in Inazuma, introduced in Version 2.2. It was blanketed in a fog that could not be removed, and is scattered with ruins and Electro hazards.

It features in the Through the Mists world quest series: it is one of three places where a perch must be given an offering during A Particularly Particular Author, and the plains are visited again in the final quest, The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna.

Geography: Autake Plains lies on Tsurumi Island, a stormy, mist-bound island off Inazuma. Its terrain is open plains broken by ruins, with Lightning Strike Probes, Electro Cubes, Ruins Torches, Phase Gates, Mysterious Carvings and Stormstones, plus Thunder Barriers and Thunder Sakura Boughs. Fluorescent Fungus is its local specialty.

Dangers: Hilichurls (including Electro and Hydro samachurls and shooters), slimes and Whopperflowers roam the plains. Elite threats include Electro and Pyro Abyss Mages, Crackling Axe Mitachurls, Thundercraven and Rockfond Rifthounds and ruin machines (Ruin Cruisers and Destroyers).

Quests: In A Particularly Particular Author, the Traveler follows a trail of mist-bound offerings and must make an offering at three perches: Chirai Shrine, Shirikoro Peak and Autake Plains. In The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna, the fourth and last Through the Mists quest, the Traveler fights Thundercraven Rifthounds here before moving on to Mt. Kanna.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Autake Plains is clear of fog and unchanged since 2.2.

14.content:
Bantan Sango Detective Agency (also: Bantan Sango, Sango Detective Agency, Everything Sango Detective Agency): The Bantan Sango Detective Agency is a private detective office in Hanamizaka, the suburb of Inazuma City north of the river. It is run by the detective Sango, who is its manager and president, with Ryuuji as her assistant. Its advertisement board promises to investigate anything on a client's behalf, from missing persons and pets to marital investigations, commercial commissions, procurement and delivery.

The name in Japanese reads roughly "Everything Sango Detective Agency", which fits its pitch. Sango says it handles murder, banditry, affair investigations and pet searches alike, warns that the fees are not cheap and should be ready before anyone walks in, and adds that she does not make empty promises. Sango does the thinking and Ryuuji does the legwork.

Places: The agency stands in the eastern part of Hanamizaka, east of the Amenoma Smithy. An advertisement board outside lists its services, and Sango receives clients inside.

People: Sango handles analysis. She says gathering intelligence is Ryuuji's job and that she waits for the clues and works through them, and she objects hotly if anyone calls that slacking. Her advice to clients is blunt: emotion is the enemy of truth, and anyone not ready to bear the truth should not cross the threshold of wisdom lightly. Ryuuji handles the physical side, collecting evidence and clues and scouting places to confirm her deductions; he admits his strength is running errands rather than stealth.

History: No founding date or earlier history is given for the agency. Ryuuji's frame-up and Sango's rescue of him happened earlier still, with no date stated. When the Traveler says they are looking for a family member lost to an unknown deity, Sango calls it a worthwhile case for the agency.

Quests: The agency appears in the repeatable "Bantan Sango Case File" commissions and, in version 2.3, in the Warrior Dog event.

Atmosphere: A small, businesslike detective office in a working suburb. Sango's manner is brisk and tart, Ryuuji comes and goes on errands, and clients are told to lean in close rather than let anyone eavesdrop on critical information.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the agency is open and unchanged: Sango still runs it and Ryuuji still works for her.

15.comment: Bantan Sango Detective Agency: Sango, the Detective
15.content: Sango is the competent, short-tempered president of the Bantan Sango Detective Agency, a woman in ordinary Inazuman dress who solves cases by reasoning from the clues Ryuuji brings her. She charges high fees and says she does not make empty promises. This entry records only her role at the agency; her own page carries her personality in more detail.

16.comment: Bantan Sango Detective Agency: Ryuuji, the Assistant
16.content: Ryuuji is Sango's assistant, a former doushin framed and suspended from the Police Station, whose name Sango cleared. He is capable in a fight and good at errands, less so at stealth. His real name is Takeo, which Sango thinks too soft; he lets her call him Ryuuji. He sees his work as supporting Sango's reasoning with his own physical effort.

17.comment: Bantan Sango Detective Agency: Bantan Sango Case Files - The Warrior Dog
17.content: During a limited-time event in version 2.3 (7 to 20 December 2021), the Bantan Sango Detective Agency posted a commission at the Adventurers' Guild for help with a mysterious case: the mass disappearance of small animals. Players rescued the animals with a gadget called the Ubiquity Net while sneaking past patrolling Canine Bunshin. The event unlocked in four segments and required Adventure Rank 30 and the Archon Quest "The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia". The event is canon but was limited, so most people in Inazuma would not know its details.

key: Village of the People of the Deep
18.content:
Bourou Village (also: Village of the People of the Deep): Bourou Village is an ancient village on Watatsumi Island, the far island of Inazuma opposite Narukami. Its people are said to have come from Enkanomiya deep beneath the waves, and it became a rallying point for those opposed to the Vision Hunt Decree. The village served as a camp where the Watatsumi Army's soldiers trained during its fight against the Shogunate.

It is an everyday village of farmers, merchants, a pharmacist and Sangonomiya Samurai, led by the elder Komaki, a fortune-teller. Kokomi's government runs the island, and the village is part of her army's base of support.

Geography: Bourou Village stands on Watatsumi Island, whose dense foliage and unusual colours set it apart from the rest of Inazuma. The Sangonomiya Shrine is the island's heart, among mountains and waterfalls. The village has an upper and lower level, and a Waverider waypoint lies south of it.

Places: The wiki's NPC list splits the village into a lower level, where most residents live, and a smaller upper level. A merchant, Kiyoko, and a pharmacist, Nishikino Reirei, work in the lower village.

People: Komaki is the village elder, an old woman who tells fortunes and tends Spiritherbs. Many villagers are Sangonomiya Samurai of the Watatsumi Army, such as Hiroyuki, Koyama, Matsuda, Ookubo Daisuke, Raku, Kagawa and Nami. The rest include Kiyoko, Mirai, Momoko and Shirai.

Governance: The island is led by the Sangonomiya Clan, whose Divine Priestess Kokomi commands the Watatsumi Army. Under the Decree it was in open opposition to the Shogunate; the Shogunate called its fighters "rebels".

Culture: The islanders worship the Watatsumi Omikami rather than the Raiden Shogun. Komaki's fortune-telling and Spiritherbs are local traditions, and Komaki says that the village has seen more history than most places, though not as much as Sangonomiya Shrine.

History: The Watatsumi Army trained soldiers at Bourou during its fight against the Shogunate. The village was a rallying point for those who feared losing their Visions or opposed the Vision Hunt Decree.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Bourou Village is calm; the army patrols as peacekeepers and the village lives on.

The Decree is gone, but the island has retained its army while the negotiations over return to Shogunate rule are unfinished. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 plot touches the village.

19.content: Watatsumi Island lies farthest from Narukami Island and is known for plants with unusual colours. Its name comes from a phrase in the ancient Watatsumi language for the god of the oceans. The Sangonomiya Clan leads the people, who worship the Watatsumi Omikami.

20.content: The Watatsumi Army, also called the resistance, is led by Sangonomiya Kokomi and opposes the Vision Hunt Decree. It includes people who feared losing or had lost their Visions, and others who simply opposed the Decree. After the Decree ended, it remains as peacekeepers, helps rebuild the island's economy and works to clear the Fatui from Watatsumi Island.

21.content:
Byakko Plain (also: Byakko no Ya, White Fox Plain, White Fox Plains): Byakko Plain is a low, sparsely wooded field in the southwest of Narukami Island, Inazuma. The main road from Konda Village to Inazuma City runs through its centre, and wild kitsune can be found near the city's outskirts. Its name means "White Fox Plain".

It is the countryside just outside Inazuma City: roadside notices, a few vendors, farming folk and foxes. The small festival island of Amakane Island lies off its western coast.

Geography: Low, open and thinly wooded, the plain occupies the southwest of Narukami Island. Its road links Konda Village with Inazuma City, and a shoreline path runs from it to Chinju Forest. Sakura Bloom grows here as a local specialty.

People: The wiki lists the NPCs Kid Kujirai and Yasuda, and the vendors Kujirai Momiji and Wakamurasaki.

Culture: The in-game expedition description says wild foxes will not appear before a traveller whose fate is not entwined with theirs twice, and that a bushy tail vanishing over the horizon is a sign of a final farewell. It is a folk saying about kitsune rather than a rule of canon.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Byakko Plain is unchanged.

key: The Sacred Forest in the Moonlight
22.content:
Chinju Forest (also: Chinju no Mori, The Sacred Forest in the Moonlight): Chinju Forest is a sacred grove in a small river valley just south of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island, and the path to the Kamisato Estate runs through it. For some unknown reason it is shrouded in perpetual night, with the glow of an unseen moon. Tanuki statues, torii gates and abandoned shrines are scattered among the trees, and legend says mischievous beings play pranks on walkers.

It is the home of the bake-danuki Ioroi, once its protector, and the setting of the "tanuki-bayashi" legend: strange drumming and music in the woods said to be made by tanuki. It was once said to be the home of many demons.

Geography: A wooded valley at the foot of Mt. Yougou, with a river running through it and paths climbing toward a big tanuki statue. Stone torii and lanterns mark routes and barriers; the forest itself sits in fixed moonlight.

Places: The tanuki statues: stone figures all over the forest, including a large one in which Ioroi was sealed. The torii gates and lanterns that mark the ritual site. Abandoned shrines hidden deep in the trees.

People: Ioroi, a bake-danuki titled the Hidden Protector of the Grove, speaks through the big statue; three small tanuki, Shousei, Kichiboushi and Gyoubu Koban, hide in the forest and are found by the Traveler. The shrine maiden Hanachirusato sends the Traveler here.

History: Legend says the forest was once home to many demons. Ioroi used to compete with the Kitsune Saiguu; after Ei nearly killed him for trying to pluck a Naku Weed from the Tenshukaku garden on Saiguu's challenge, Saiguu pleaded for him and the Shogun put him under her command as Protector of the Grove.

Quests: Tanuki-Bayashi in the Forest, part of Cleansing Defilement within the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual series: the Traveler finds the tanuki, receives Ioroi's Ward and breaks the barrier, defeating an Ochimusha.

Dangers: Hilichurls, an Electro Cicin Mage and an Ochimusha spirit tied to the barrier. Otherwise a gentle forest; its main hazard is getting lost to pranks.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the forest is unchanged: moonlit, quiet and full of tanuki statues, with Ioroi still in his stone.

No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content has altered it. The Cleansing Defilement quest's rituals are complete, so the barriers are down.

23.comment: Chinju Forest: Ioroi and the Tanuki-Bayashi
23.content: Ioroi is a bake-danuki who lives in Chinju Forest and calls Saiguu 'that sneaky kitsune'. He first mistook the Traveler for a fellow tanuki and, on realising they were human, panicked and sent hilichurls to drive them off. He agreed to give up the comb and ward only if the Traveler played with three young tanuki. His seal leaves him unable to move; he relies on reports from tanuki who were not petrified.

24.content:
Chirai Shrine (also: Chirai Shaden): Chirai Shrine is a stretch of ruined shrine buildings on Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. It is one of the three places on the fog-bound island where a Perch must receive offerings in the world quest A Particularly Particular Author, and its ruins hide a door into the Tsurumi Underground Ruins.

Hilichurls, Samachurls and ruin machines now roam the stones. The island once belonged to the Thunderbird Civilization, whose people lived under the Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir, and a Perch on a small islet north-east of the ruins is a relic of their rites.

Geography: Ruins and hills on Tsurumi Island, with a Perch on a small island to the north-east. Features include Electro Cubes, Electro Current puzzles and Phase Gates, and Fluorescent Fungus grows locally. A door under the ruins leads down to the basement and on into the Tsurumi Underground Ruins.

History: Chirai Shrine sits on land of the Thunderbird Civilization, an ancient people who worshipped the Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir. Canon does not describe the shrine itself. Its Perch belongs to the offering ceremony that the island's time loop still replays.

Dangers: Hilichurls with wooden shields, Electro Hilichurl Shooters, Hydro and Electro Samachurls, Electro Whopperflowers, and elite Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Ruin Cruisers and Ruin Defenders. The Hydro Samachurl group and the Ruin Scouts change positions over a three-day cycle.

Travel: The island's fog blocks exploration until the Through the Mists quest series is under way; a gate in the first quest lifts part of it. The Chirai Perch is reached by following feathers through a Phase Gate and across the ruins.

Quests: A Particularly Particular Author (2.2): the Traveler makes offerings at the Perch here, one of three, as commissioned by the island's locals who are really illusions of the past. Gameplay note: the feather route involves defeating two Electro Whopperflowers and Thundercraven Rifthound Whelps.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine is ruined and populated only by monsters; the island's curse and fog were lifted in Version 2.2 and no later content changes the place.

25.content: The Perches are offering sites used in the Thunderbird Civilization's ceremony. In A Particularly Particular Author Ruu makes a clumsy offering to one and the Traveler completes three: at Chirai Shrine, Shirikoro Peak and the Autake Plains. In later quest steps the Traveler destroys them to stop the ceremony, a spoiler for The Sea of Fog and the Rite of the Trees.

26.content:
Court of Flowing Sand: Court of Flowing Sand is a Domain of Forgery on the north side of Mt. Yougou, Narukami Island, Inazuma. Its description says that in antediluvian times, now lost to history, a foolish ruler dreamed of building a high garden in honour of the white sacred tree over the primordial sands; now a dead silence fills the kingdom built on sand, but the obsessions of the past remain.

Clearing it yields Weapon Ascension Materials (the Branches of a Distant Sea, Narukami's Magatamas and Oni Masks series, which rotate by weekday). It was added in Version 2.0 with the Inazuma region.

Geography: A golden-sand altar where dust 'flows into eternity', on the north side of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island. The mountain is also the site of the Sacred Sakura.

Dangers: Slimes of several elements (Hydro, Pyro, Electro), Abyss Mages, Electro Hilichurl Grenadiers and Crackling Axe Mitachurls, depending on the challenge level.

History: Canon says nothing beyond the rumour in the description: an unnamed ruler in an age before the great flood wished to raise a high garden for the white tree over the primordial sands. Treat it as legend.

27.content:
Dainichi Mikoshi (also: Great Sun Mikoshi, Helios, Hyperion, Byakuya no Hikari, Oohirume no Omikoshi): The Dainichi Mikoshi ("Great Sun Mikoshi") is the artificial sun of Enkanomiya, the hidden realm of Inazuma. The ancient craftsman-sage Aberaku no Mikoto made it to protect the people of Byakuyakoku from the Dragonheirs of the Depths, now called Bathysmal Vishaps. When it burns the realm is in Whitenight, and when it is dark, in Evernight; mechanisms around Enkanomiya can toggle the two. The structure and the ground around it form a subarea of the realm.

Aberaku privately called his creation Helios, the solar chariot that drives Hyperion; before Inazuman Watatsumi culture took hold it was known as Hyperion (Byakuya no Hikari). Its history is not purely heroic: nobles later turned the sun into a god to be worshipped and ruled in the name of a child, the Sunchild.

Geography: The Dainichi Mikoshi stands at the heart of Enkanomiya and works as its main light source, with a central teleport waypoint beneath it and hidden rooms below. Floating rocks above it let a glider reach three nearby loci without falling into the depths. Its surroundings are crowded with Ruin Guards, Hilichurl camps and Abyss mages, and a barrier blocks its approach early in The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent.

History: When Byakuyakoku sank into the sea, the Dragonheirs of the Depths tormented its people. The Heavenly Principles and three of their four Shades did not answer the people's pleas; only Istaroth heard and taught Aberaku enough to build the Mikoshi. Its light drove the Dragonheirs away, Whitenight came, Evernight was banished, and the first year of Sun and Moon began. In the second year a cabal of corrupt nobles led the people to worship the Mikoshi as a god and installed a child puppet ruler, the Sunchild. Aberaku opposed this, was accused of treason by the Sunchild and imprisoned, and died in the tenth year of Sun and Moon. His clothes, crown and bones were enshrined in separate places, which split his soul into fragments.

Quests: The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent is the quest that opens Enkanomiya's deeper story and is required before Hyperion's Dirge and Lotus Eater. Hyperion's Dirge begins with Aberaku beneath the central waypoint and ends at the top of the structure. Three smaller inquiries (Narrow, Temple and Serpent's Heart) gather his relics in The Narrows, the Evernight Temple and the Serpent's Heart.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Dainichi Mikoshi still serves as Enkanomiya's sun and can be toggled between Whitenight and Evernight.

No 6.x or 7.x content found on the wiki touches it. In Hyperion's Dirge the Traveler's task is to reunite the fragments of Aberaku's soul.

28.content: Whitenight is the bright half of Enkanomiya's cycle, kept by the Dainichi Mikoshi; Evernight is its dark opposite. Their rule is that the Mikoshi can be turned on and off to switch them, using mechanisms spread through the realm that unlock as quests are completed. The two states also hide and reveal different things, such as Ruins Torches that show as Sunfire Phantasms by day. The ancients called the era after the sun's creation the years of Sun and Moon.

29.content:
Depths of Mt. Yougou (also: Mt. Yougou: The Depths, Depths of Mount Yougou): The Depths of Mt. Yougou is the dark space beneath Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island where the central roots of the Sacred Sakura lie. Its plants have grown gnarled and unnatural in utter darkness, and something twisted was sealed there. It is opened only at the end of the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual, when the barrier is lifted and the Miasmic Tumor made of the roots' accumulated filth is destroyed.

"Depths of Mt. Yougou" is an unofficial name; the quest map calls it Mt. Yougou: The Depths.

Geography: The Depths are a cave reached through an opening at the roots of the Sacred Sakura, beneath the Grand Narukami Shrine's mountain. A large pool of Electrified Water beside the mountain drains health until the ritual is done. The final quest sends the Traveler jumping into the opening beside Hanachirusato.

History: The Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual has to clear the central roots in the Depths of Mt. Yougou as its last stage, after the barriers at the Thunder Sakura roots have been broken and the filth purged. The filth here condenses into a Miasmic Tumor. The most recent time this was done was by the Traveler and Hanachirusato.

Quests: The Depths feature in Yougou Cleansing, the final part of the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual series. After the tumor is purged, Hanachirusato reveals herself to be filth condensed from the memory of the Kitsune Saiguu and must be cleansed too, so she dissipates after saying goodbye, leaving behind a mask. Completing it grants the achievement Spring Cleaning.

Dangers: The Miasmic Tumor and the Ochimusha that appear during its fight; before the ritual is completed, the Electrified Water around the mountain's foot.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Depths are cleansed. No 6.x or 7.x story content about them was found on the wiki.

The Electrified Water pool is de-energised and the Sacred Sakura now glows blue.

30.comment: Depths of Mt. Yougou: Miasmic Tumor
30.content: The Miasmic Tumor is the physical form the accumulated defilement of the Sacred Sakura's roots takes in the Depths of Mt. Yougou during the major cleansing. Left alone, tainted roots could corrode and kill the tree, so it must be destroyed by whoever performs the ritual.

31.content:
Dragonbone Flower (also: Dragonbone Orb, Fretnaught Fruit): The Dragonbone Flower is a giant flower in the Serpent's Bowels of Enkanomiya. During the world quest Lotus Eater, the Traveler waters it with the Waters of Lethe from Tokoyo Reisen, and after a wait it condenses into a Dragonbone Orb: a fruit whose scent calms the mind and sweeps worries away. Its story is a warning that comfort can dull the will to resist.

The orb is how the last members of a Byakuyakoku resistance tried to fund themselves, and how that resistance lost its fighting spirit. Bards in Mondstadt are said to call the orb the "Fretnaught Fruit".

Quests: In Lotus Eater (a world quest started near the Serpent's Heart, reached during Evernight) a spirit at the altar has forgotten his own name. The Traveler learns from a stone tablet that he is Supada no Hiko, also called Spartacus, and he sends them to find his surviving students. One of them, Adonis, hides in The Narrows and explains the orbs; as thanks he reveals that they can only be made with the waters of Lethe from Tokoyo Reisen. The Traveler pours the water on the flower from its top, then returns after the next daily reset to take the orb.

Atmosphere: A strange, hushed bloom in the dim depths of Enkanomiya, tied to Lethe, the water of forgetting. The mood is soporific and bittersweet rather than threatening.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the flower remains in Enkanomiya's Serpent's Bowels, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes its story.

32.content:
End of the Oneiric Euthymia: End of the Oneiric Euthymia is a Trounce Domain on Mt. Yougou, Narukami Island, Inazuma. It is unlocked after Transient Dreams, the second act of the Raiden Shogun's Story Quest (Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter), and lets players relive the battle against Magatsu Mitake Narukami no Mikoto, called the Shogun, as a memory. Its description says dreams once blew about like petals, never fulfilled; this is the origin of Eternity, and also 'her' end.

Version 2.5 added both the quest and the domain. Rewards are weekly-boss-style materials (Mudra of the Malefic General, Tears of the Calamitous God, The Meaning of Aeons) and Vajrada Amethyst gems.

Geography: The domain sits on Mt. Yougou, where the Sacred Sakura grows. Its quest version is fought during the quest steps Farewell to the Past and Radiant Sakura.

Dangers: A single boss, Magatsu Mitake Narukami no Mikoto. She absorbs 'Ominous Destiny'; when it fills she enters the Baleful Shadowlord form, which drains active characters' Energy and resists damage.

History: The wiki's quest summary has Ei confronting her past and her views on eternity with the Traveler's help, after rifthounds attacked the Sacred Sakura's roots. The domain replays the Shogun fight from that quest.

33.content:
Enkanomiya (also: Tokoyokoku, Delphi Pytho, Palace Below the Depths): Enkanomiya is a sunken realm deep beneath Watatsumi Island in Inazuma, entered through a pool beside Sangonomiya Shrine. Once a surface nation called Delphi Pytho, it fell into the depths during the ancient war of funerary flame and became Tokoyokoku, then Byakuyakoku, lit only by an artificial sun, the Dainichi Mikoshi. The Watatsumi people descend from its inhabitants, whom the serpent god Orobashi led back to the surface. Today it is an empty ruin of ghostly Shades of Tokoyo and hostile Bathysmal Vishaps.

Its name means "Palace Below the Depths". The artificial sun can be switched off, flipping the realm between bright Whitenight and dark Evernight. Its old records, including the forbidden chronicle Before Sun and Moon, preserve a version of world history that is otherwise almost lost.

Geography: A dark undersea expanse with no mountains, in which ruined islands, terraces and temples float or stand amid open darkness; the Dainichi Mikoshi rises at the centre. Main subareas: Dainichi Mikoshi, The Narrows, The Serpent's Heart and Evernight Temple, plus The Serpent's Bowels near the entrance and three hidden islands at the realm's corners (Yachimatahiko's Locus, Yachimatahime's Locus and Kunado's Locus).

Places: Dainichi Mikoshi: the artificial sun, once called Helios or Hyperion. The Serpent's Heart: anciently Delphi, "land of snakes", built to guard secrets, hold prisoners and worship the cosmic serpent Ouroboros; its altar is a sealing device. Evernight Temple: holds the Tokoyo Reisen, a stream once called the River Lethe. The Narrows: a long, widened passage. The three Loci: islands on which stood the hidden Towers of the Three Realms.

People: No living community remains; the Enkanomiyans moved to Watatsumi Island long ago, and some great Watatsumi houses, such as the Yuna Clan, trace their lines back to Byakuyakoku. The "inhabitants" now are Shades of Tokoyo (Sinshades): afterimages of past people's memories and feelings that appear during Evernight, among them the sage Aberaku, the seven Sunchildren, the shrine maiden Eboshi (Erebos) and Aru, a "sinless" shade made to help with the Watatsumi ritual.

History: As Delphi Pytho it belonged to the single unified human civilization that followed the Primordial One's victory over the Seven Sovereigns. When the "second throne of the heavens" (Nibelung) returned and the war of funerary flame broke out about 6,000 years ago, the land fell into the depths. In the darkness the Dragonheirs of the Depths (Bathysmal Vishaps) preyed on the people, and lanterns could not hold them back. Only Istaroth answered their prayers, enlightening the sage Abrax (Aberaku), who led the building of Helios, the Dainichi Mikoshi; its light drove the vishaps off and began the "Years of Sun and Moon". The people then found their way to the surface barred, and nobles installed the puppet Sunchildren. Ages later a child found the fugitive god Orobashi in a cave and asked it to be their god; Orobashi overthrew the Sunchildren, sealed away the vishaps and grew a coral path to the surface, creating Watatsumi Island, to which the people migrated.

Travel: Enkanomiya is sealed from Watatsumi Island by five Goshou Rocks, the Eye, Fang (Tooth), Fin, Tail and Heart. The Spirit Pearls from the first four unlock the Heart, which yields the Key of the Moon-Bathed Deep, said to be forged from Orobashi's blood. With the spirit veins between the realms flowing and a bearer "as clear as water", the key opens the deep pool directly across from (east of) Sangonomiya Shrine, the Moon-Bathed Deep, into the descent.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Enkanomiya remains an empty, sealed ruin beneath Watatsumi, visited mainly by the Traveler. Its people's descendants live on Watatsumi Island.

The Traveler retrieved the Bloodbranch Coral for the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri and defeated Enjou, but the Abyss Order knows the place. No later Archon Quest returns there, and it is little known outside Inazuma: when the Traveler mentions it in Fontaine, Wriothesley has never heard of it and had meant to ask Neuvillette about it.

34.comment: Enkanomiya: Dainichi Mikoshi, Whitenight and Evernight
34.content: The Dainichi Mikoshi ("Great Sun Mikoshi") is Enkanomiya's artificial sun, a tower of three tall pillars around a triangular interior at the realm's centre. Built by the sage Aberaku (Abrax), who called it Helios, "the divine chariot of the sun", it was later known as Hyperion. Its light drove off the Dragonheirs and created Whitenight; with it switched off, the realm returns to Evernight, when hidden walls, mechanisms and shades appear. Nobles later made it an object of worship, and the Sunchildren's Rite of Solar Return took place in its inner sanctum.

35.content: The Sunchildren (Phaethons) were child rulers whom a noble cabal set up and manipulated after the Dainichi Mikoshi was built. There were seven: Rikoru (the first), Ion, Isumenasu, Orupeusu, Piramumon, Risutaiosu and Surepio. They were hated for the cruelties done in their name, though people knew they were puppets. Their attendants were forbidden to speak to them, and before a Sunchild grew old enough to see the truth, the Rite of Solar Return burned the child to death inside the artificial sun. The Divine Bridle was the badge of their office. Orobashi ended their rule. Their shades can still be found in Evernight.

36.content: Aberaku no Mikoto (originally Abrax) was the sage who, enlightened by Tokoyo Ookami (Istaroth), designed the Dainichi Mikoshi and led its construction. When he saw how the nobles used the Sunchild, they convinced Rikoru that Aberaku wanted his throne; he was charged with high treason and held in a high, dark, cold prison for the rest of his life, dying by the tenth year of Sun and Moon. His enshrined bones, crown and robes split his shade into fragments; the Traveler reunited them in "Hyperion's Dirge". Proud and theatrical, he introduces himself as "Helios-Forger" and bears no hatred for the child who imprisoned him.

37.content: Because Byakuyakoku is a "nether realm", it sometimes projects afterimages of the past from people's lingering thoughts: the Shades of Tokoyo or Sinshades, ley line phenomena born of strong feelings called "Sins of Tokoyo". It is said that when the God of Moments looks with favour on someone, their feelings and memories remain forever. They appear only in Evernight. Ancient Enkanomiyans called both these and the mirages of Whitenight "Eidolons", and only after Orobashi came did they tell them apart as Ghostfire Phantasms and Sunfire Phantasms. A shade that realises what it is soon fades.

38.content: The Bathysmal Vishaps, called Dragonheirs of the Depths, are deep-sea vishaps that held the depths when Byakuyakoku fell and hunted its people in the dark. They shun man-made light; one in-game description says this is because they were robbed of the true sun and the surface. They are proud elemental creatures that never bowed to any god and can adapt fast, passing chosen traits and new elements to their young within a generation.

39.comment: Enkanomiya: Towers of the Three Realms and Eboshi
39.content: At Byakuyakoku's three corners stood towers that harmonised the three realms meeting there and steadied the land's winds and waters. They were so important that they were hidden by secret arts, summonable only by shrine maidens and Vassals of Watatsumi; their ancient names are lost, and the islands are now called Yachimatahiko's, Yachimatahime's and Kunado's Locus. The shade of Eboshi (Erebos), a shrine maiden and auxiliary of Sangonomiya, raises them and sets the Traveler three martial trials after the Bloodbranch Coral reaches Watatsumi ("Erebos' Secret").

40.content: Defeated in the Archon War, the serpent god Orobashi fled the continent and ended up in a cavern of the depths. A child of Enkanomiya, diving past the three corners on a dare to look for a Dragonbone Flower, found it and felt kinship rather than fear. Calling itself the Profane Serpent with no mortal followers left, it agreed to become their god. It overthrew the Sunchildren, sealed the Dragonheirs, taught the people, and broke off its own coral branches to give them light and build a ladder to the surface, the origin of Watatsumi Island. Its life force lives on in the Bloodbranch Coral.

41.content: Before Sun and Moon is an Enkanomiyan chronicle, forbidden to ordinary readers, mixing fable and history from the world's beginning to the building of the Dainichi Mikoshi; it is Vol. 2 of The Byakuyakoku Collection. It tells how the first throne of the heavens, the Primordial One (possibly Phanes), defeated the Seven Sovereigns, made four shining shades, and created humanity, with whom it made a covenant; how the second throne came and the funerary war cast Delphi Pytho into the depths; and how only Istaroth heard the people. Its scribe stops writing in the Tenth Year of Sun and Moon on hearing armour outside.

42.content: In Enkanomiya the Traveler meets Enjou, a polite man who claims to be clerical staff assisting the trial and explains that the place's true name is Byakuyakoku. He helps them break into the Dainichi Mikoshi, but is really an Abyss Order agent searching for records from before the artificial sun; after the vishaps beneath the tower fall, he reveals himself as an Abyss Lector, fights the Traveler, and leaves after hinting that Paimon may someday betray them. He later reappears in Natlan under other names.

43.comment: Enkanomiya: Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri and the descent
43.content: By legend the depths of Enkanomiya pull at Watatsumi's spirit every few thousand years, bleaching the soil into infertile Holy Soil. The Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri pushes the spirits back down using a Jade Coral Branch (Bloodbranch Coral) broken off in the depths, said to be made from Orobashi's own body. The shrine maiden Tsuyuko, who studied at the Sumeru Akademiya, believes seawater salinity causes the bleaching and that the coral's nutrients restore the land. She recruited the Traveler to break the Goshou Rock seals and, with Kokomi's permission, fetch the coral.

44.comment: Enkanomiya: Aphotic Diffusal (Three Realms Gateway Offering)
44.content: During the limited-time event "Three Realms Gateway Offering" (2.5), a darkness laced with abyssal energy engulfed Enkanomiya and complicated the Watatsumi ritual. Kokomi sent the Traveler back down, where they met Tsumi, a snake-masked shrine maiden who had been tending wounded Watatsumi soldiers. Enjou had promised the vishaps the darkness they craved in exchange for safe passage for the Abyss Order, then rebuilt the towers to spread a darkness poisonous even to them. The Traveler dispelled it and persuaded Tsumi, who was raised by the vishaps and could have destroyed the Dainichi Mikoshi, not to do so; she warned that the vishaps would return. Back at the shrine, Kokomi took Tsumi to be the last Vassal of Watatsumi (Orobashi's half-serpent familiars), rejected Enjou's theory that she was one of the "vishap-people" (Reptilians: vishaps that imitate humans and differ only in their vertical pupils) as pure fiction, since Watatsumi's ancient documents say nothing of them, and resolved to find a way to stop the soil bleaching that would not keep disturbing the vishaps.

45.content:
Evernight Temple (also: Tokoyo Reibyou): The Evernight Temple is a subarea of Enkanomiya, the sunken ancient land reached from beneath Watatsumi Island. It is a ruined sacred site where a faintly glowing stream, the Tokoyo Reisen (once called the River Lethe), runs close by. Offerings, hidden rooms and spectral figures from old Byakuyakoku are scattered through it, among them a fragment of the dead inventor Aberaku.

Enkanomiya shifts between "Whitenight" and "Evernight" with the Dainichi Mikoshi, and some barriers, rooms and spirits at the temple exist only in one phase. Its Japanese name is written 常夜霊廟; the wiki glosses it as "Evernight Mausoleum".

Geography: Enkanomiya lies under Watatsumi Island and is entered through a deep pool east of Sangonomiya Shrine once the seals on the five Goshou Rocks are broken. The Evernight Temple is one of its subareas, a glide down from the eastern teleport waypoint of the Dainichi Mikoshi. It holds an Elemental Monument, Triangular Mechanisms, Places of Essence Worship and Seelie, and its local specialty is Sea Ganoderma. A quiet coral-ringed open space near the temple is one of the sitting spots in a hidden objective.

Places: The Tokoyo Reisen, the stream beside the temple, marked as its own point of interest. A secret room, reached by following the traces of Bathysmal Vishaps, which holds one fragment of the Reins of Revival. The precinct where part of Aberaku's remains (his "sacred crown") was enshrined.

People: There are no living residents. Spectral figures appear in Evernight: the spirit of Aberaku, who calls himself Helios-Forger, and seven Sunchildren (Ion, Isumenasu, Orupeusu, Piramumon, Rikoru, Risutaiosu and Surepio), who can be spoken to only in Evernight and vanish afterwards. The Sunchildren were child figureheads of old Byakuyakoku, ruled through by a cabal of nobles.

History: Enkanomiya (earlier Byakuyakoku, Tokoyokoku, and originally Delphi Pytho) sank into the sea in the war of funerary flame and was cut off from the surface. Its people held off the Dragonheirs of the Depths, now called Bathysmal Vishaps, with the Dainichi Mikoshi, the artificial sun Aberaku built. Corrupt nobles later set up child Sunchildren as puppet rulers; Aberaku, who opposed them, was imprisoned on the first Sunchild's accusation and died in captivity, and his clothes and body were enshrined in several places. The crown was kept at the Evernight Temple. Orobashi later overthrew the Sunchildren and led the survivors up to the surface.

Quests: Temple Inquiry (Hyperion's Dirge): Aberaku's spirit-trial is passed here and the Offerings of the Temple are collected. The Trail of Drake and Serpent (From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku): Vishap traces lead to a secret room and a fragment of the Reins of Revival. Sunchildren Hide and Seek: a hidden objective unlocked after The Phaethons' Syrtos. Lotus Eater: the Waters of Lethe are drawn from the Tokoyo Reisen.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the temple stands unchanged in Enkanomiya, explorable and empty of living people. Nothing newer than its 2.4 content was found.

Enkanomiya itself is little known outside Inazuma; when the Traveler mentioned it to Wriothesley in Fontaine, he had to ask what it was.

46.comment: Evernight Temple: Tokoyo Reisen and the Waters of Lethe
46.content: The Tokoyo Reisen is a stream at the temple, once called the River Lethe. Its water shines faintly and does not by itself make a drinker forget, but the Dragonbone Orb, a rare fruit that a Dragonbone Flower bears when watered with it, calms the mind and sweeps worries away. In the Lotus Eater quest Adonis, a student of the resistance leader Supada no Hiko (called Spartacus), says remnants of the resistance sold the orbs to fund their cause; many fighters then lost their will to resist, and he wonders if the formula was planted by the nobles who ruled through the Sunchildren.

47.comment: Evernight Temple: Aberaku at the Evernight Temple
47.content: In the Temple Inquiry, Aberaku's spirit calls himself "Helios-Forger" and does not remember how he died, only that a child ordered his imprisonment and that he feels no hatred for that child, who was a puppet. He asks the Traveler to defeat the monsters that act as warders of his spirit, and hands over the Offerings of the Temple, which hold part of his thoughts. His speech keeps breaking off mid-thought.

48.comment: Evernight Temple: The Sunchildren of the Temple
48.content: The Sunchildren (Phaethons) were child figureheads of Byakuyakoku after the Dainichi Mikoshi was built; a cabal of corrupt nobles used them as puppets and let them take the blame for harm done in their name. When a Sunchild reached a certain age the Rite of Solar Return ended that Sunchild's life, so they could not realise they were being manipulated. Rikoru was the first Sunchild. In the Sunchildren Hide and Seek objective seven of them are found as afterimages at the temple. Describe them factually and gently: lonely children of an unjust system.

49.content:
Fort Fujitou (also: Fujitou-toride, Wisteria Helmet Fort): Fort Fujitou is a Watatsumi Army camp on Yashiori Island, where soldiers of the Sangonomiya resistance, led by Sangonomiya Kokomi, held ground against the Shogunate's forces. It sits among thunderstorms and the Tatarigami-stricken land of the island. The Traveler meets the officer Kaida Ryouma and the blacksmith Miyazaki Saburou there, and a man named Kaji who starts the Orobashi's Legacy quests.

The Japanese name means "Wisteria Helmet Fort". After Kokomi's story quest the background soldiers leave the camp, and by then the resistance has become a peace-keeping and rebuilding body.

Geography: On Yashiori Island, beside the electric weather of the island, with an Electro Cube, Electro Rock Pile, Electro Seelie, Narukami Pillar, Thunder Barrier and Thunder Sakura Bough around it. Local specialty: Crystal Marrow.

People: Kaida Ryouma is a Sangonomiya officer who used to work for the Kujou Clan and fought against them. Miyazaki Saburou is a swordsmith from Tatarasuna, a successor of the Miyazaki Art, who joined the Army for protection and forges its arms. Others include the samurai Moriguchi, Nathan and Takahashi, and the workers Sumi and Yuuzou. Kaji moves to the Kujou Encampment after Orobashi's Legacy.

Governance: Military camp run under Kokomi and General Gorou. Kokomi is the leader; Gorou is the general; Ryouma is an officer. The Army is called "rebels" by the Shogunate.

History: During the Vision Hunt Decree war, the camp was a staging post for the resistance. Kaji arrives there to look into the Yashiori storms, which he ties to the destroyed wards and the remains of Orobashi. After the Traveler persuades the Raiden Shogun to change course, the Decree ends, and peace talks begin; Ryouma says soldiers there are glad, and the Army keeps order and helps rebuild.

Quests: Orobashi's Legacy (Kaji's quests, Parts I to V) begins here; Kokomi's story quest Warriors' Dreams Like Spring Grass Renewing ends the war's aftermath.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the camp is still a Watatsumi Army site, though quieter, since the Vision Hunt Decree ended and soldiers moved on to peace work.

50.comment: Fort Fujitou: Kaji and Orobashi's Legacy
50.content: Kaji, a man at Fort Fujitou, investigates the island's endless rain and lightning, which he believes comes from destroyed ancient wards linked to the slain Orobashi. The Traveler repairs wards at Musoujin Gorge, Serpent's Head and Jakotsu Mine; Fort Mumei then rises from the sea and the final ward is restored.

51.content:
Fort Hiraumi (also: Hiraumi Fort, Hiraumi-toride, Flat Sea Fort): Fort Hiraumi is a subarea at the eastern tip of Seirai Island, the Inazuman island scarred by a long-ago calamity and a perpetual thunderstorm. It is a fort-like site on the island, roamed by Nobushi, Kairagi and Treasure Hoarders and home to the Slumbering Court, a domain. The in-game map calls it Hiraumi-toride.

Nothing in the game text says who built the fort or what it once guarded. What canon shows is its present state: a stormy, lightning-charged place with Electro puzzles, Thunder Sakura Boughs and Phase Gates, with an abandoned mansion on its grounds that the domain description calls the haunt of monsters from the rift.

Geography: The fort lies on Seirai Island, the island whose centre was once wrapped in constant storm and Balethunder until the Seirai Stormchasers quests were completed. Electro runs through the whole area. Features listed for the subarea include Electro Cubes, Electro Seelie, Lightning Strike Probes, light-up tile puzzles, Thunder Barriers, Thunder Sakura Boughs, Phase Gates, a Waverider Waypoint and bake-danuki. Local specialties include Amakumo Fruit, Naku Weed and Sea Ganoderma.

Places: The main landmark is the Slumbering Court, the domain on the fort's grounds. Its official description calls it a masterless mansion that has become the haunting ground of rift monsters, and it rewards those who master its Electro trial with artifacts. A cat-shaped hidden objective, "The Cat's Affection" (an unofficial name), is located to the right of the domain and needs the recipe from the quest Neko Is a Cat: Shrine Recipe.

People: There are no named residents. The area is held by Nobushi (Hitsukeban, Jintouban and Kikouban), Kairagi, Treasure Hoarders, Hilichurl Shooters and Mirror Maidens among the elite enemies.

Dangers: Electro Slimes and Whopperflowers, Nobushi and Kairagi patrols, Treasure Hoarder gangs, specters, Crackling and Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Mirror Maidens and Ruin Machines (Ruin Cruisers and Scouts). Lightning-charged terrain and Thunder Barriers shape how safely anyone can move.

History: No history of the fort itself is given. The island around it is said to have suffered a calamity that left its centre in a perpetual thunderstorm.

Travel: Fort Hiraumi has a Teleport Waypoint and a Waverider Waypoint. Fort Hiraumi and Seirai Island were added in version 2.1.

Quests: The fort appears in the Seirai Stormchasers world quest series (Part III's Warding Stone route), the Neko Is a Cat shrine recipe chain, the commissions mentioned above, and a Torn Page, "Toki Alley Tales (III)", whose location is listed as east of the fort.

Atmosphere: Electro everywhere: lightning probes, Thunder Barriers and Thunder Sakura Boughs, with hostile patrols and the shadow of the haunted mansion nearby. It is an island that bears the marks of a calamity and a storm that raged for a long time.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Fort Hiraumi is an open, hostile exploration area on Seirai Island; the wiki records no change since 2.1.

52.content: The Slumbering Court is an Electro-themed domain on Seirai Island. Its in-game description calls it a masterless mansion that has become the haunting ground of monsters from the rift, and says those who can wield the eternal lightning to conquer its trial will win artifacts. Thundercraven Rifthounds are among its enemies, and Electro-Charged is the effective way to fight them. The domain's own page is the place for its gameplay detail; the lore tie to the fort is not explained.

53.content:
Fort Mumei (also: Mumyou-toride, Fort of Ignorance): Fort Mumei is a group of ruins on Yashiori Island, remains of an ancient, majestic city that fell in the Archon War when the serpent god Orobashi invaded the island and clashed with the Raiden Shogun's forces. It lay under the sea until the Traveler finished the Orobashi's Legacy quests, when the fort rose out of the water near Watatsumi Island.

Its name means "ignorance" (the Buddhist avidya) in Japanese and sounds like "nameless". The small islets nearby were often used as transit points for supplies going to Watatsumi Island.

Geography: A cluster of ruined structures on Yashiori Island near Watatsumi Island, ringed by islets. Features: Electro Seelie, a Light-Up Tile Puzzle, a Narukami Pillar, a Thunder Sakura Bough, a Waverider Waypoint, a sword hilt (from the quest Put Them To Rest), a Handy Notepad, and Sea Ganoderma. Enemies are Hilichurl Fighters, Pyro Hilichurl Shooters, Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Ruin Destroyers and Ruin Scouts.

History: Late in the Archon War, Orobashi invaded Yashiori Island and came into conflict with the Electro Archon (Beelzebul, the Raiden Shogun), which destroyed the ancient city. The Archon slew Orobashi, splitting the island and leaving the Musoujin Gorge, and set wards to hold down the Tatarigami, the slain god's lingering hatred.

Quests: Orobashi's Legacy, Parts IV and V (with Kaji): the fort rises from the sea, and the last ward is restored. The Kokomi quest Sword, Fish, Resistance mentions the ruins as a supply route near Watatsumi.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruin stands above water and the island's Tatarigami weather has calmed with its wards repaired.

54.comment: Fort Mumei: Orobashi and the Battle of Yashiori
54.content: Orobashi no Mikoto, the Watatsumi Omikami, led its forces to Yashiori Island near the end of the Archon War and fought the Electro Archon. The Archon killed it with the Musou no Hitotachi, splitting the island and creating the Musoujin Gorge. Its lingering hatred became the Tatarigami, held back by the Archon's wards. Watatsumi's people kept worshipping Orobashi.

55.content:
Hanamizaka (also: Flower-Viewing Slope, Hanamizaka district): Hanamizaka is the suburb of Inazuma City on the north side of the river that cuts through the city's northern part, one of the city's three parts alongside Tenryou and Tenshukaku. It is a district of family workshops and shops: the Naganohara fireworks shop, Amenoma Smithy, Kiminami Restaurant, Yae Publishing House and the Bantan Sango detective agency. Its name means "Flower-Viewing Slope".

Compared with the commercial street of Tenryou it feels more residential and artisan. It is where a firework-maker, a master bladesmith, a restaurant owner, a pair of detectives and a famous publisher are neighbours, and where the Shogunate's bulletin board carried everything from official notices to graffiti and complaints.

Geography: Hanamizaka lies north of the river through the north of Inazuma City, on Narukami Island. Amenoma Smithy stands at the city's eastern end, in the eastern suburb; the western outskirts hold quieter homes and a few city watchmen. The Hanamizaka bulletin board stands north-east of the city's northern Teleport Waypoint.

Places: Naganohara Fireworks: the Naganohara family's shop, run by Yoimiya's family, called by an Inazuman named Takami the oldest and one of the best in Inazuma. It also sells small toys and trinkets, some imported by the Crux fleet and some made by Yoimiya.
Amenoma Smithy: the workshop of the Amenoma Art, one of the five bladesmithing schools of the Raiden Gokaden. Amenoma Tougo owns it; his disciple Hajime handles ordinary ironware and weapons.
Kiminami Restaurant: owned by Kiminami Anna, with a menu notice advertising a new dish from abroad.
Yae Publishing House: the great publisher founded by Yae Miko, with editors in the suburb.
Bantan Sango Detective Agency: Ryuuji and Sango's agency, taking missing persons, lost pets, deliveries and procurement.

People: Notable residents of the eastern suburb: the firework-maker Naganohara Ryuunosuke, the bladesmith Amenoma Tougo, the detectives Ryuuji and Sango, and the editors Shigeru and Kuroda of Yae Publishing House. City watchmen (doushin) such as Andou and Amano and the yoriki Kurosawa Kyounosuke patrol the suburb on behalf of the Tenryou Commission.

Governance: Hanamizaka falls under the Shogunate's city administration. Order is kept by the Tenryou Commission's watchmen; festivals and ceremony fall under the Yashiro Commission, which created the first fireworks show.

Culture: Hanamizaka is where Inazuma's festival craft lives: fireworks launched for the Naganohara show, forged blades and the novels on sale. People associate fireworks with what matters to them (friendship, marriage, belief), and families pick their own fireworks through paper slips supplied by the Naganohara family.

History: Canon gives Hanamizaka no founding story. Its notable history comes from the Archon Quest era: during the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees the suburb's bulletin board and smithy notices show the war's effects, such as the stalled supply of Jade Steel, and Arataki Itto's public quarrel with the Kujou tengu.

Travel: The Hanamizaka bulletin board stands near the city's northern Teleport Waypoint. Amakane Island is the place to watch the fireworks.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Hanamizaka is an ordinary peaceful suburb; the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees are over and the shops are open.

Yoimiya's family runs the fireworks shop and show as before. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 plot touches the suburb.

56.comment: Hanamizaka: Naganohara Fireworks and the Fireworks Show
56.content: Naganohara Fireworks is the shop of the Naganohara family in Hanamizaka, said to be the oldest and one of the best in Inazuma. Yoimiya, the family's firework-maker, even had the Crux fleet fire fireworks overseas to spread its name. The shop also sells knickknacks beloved by children and adults: Scatterbloom Marbles that bloom when they strike each other, Leaping Tops that chirp like birds, Neon Dragonflies that change colour in flight, and Katydid Coils that repel mosquitos.

57.content: Amenoma Smithy is a smithy on the eastern end of Inazuma City, in Hanamizaka. Its master, Amenoma Tougo, practises the Amenoma Art, one of the five bladesmithing schools of the Raiden Gokaden, and in his old age accepts only orders for exquisite Jade Steel swords and knives. Everyday ironware and ordinary weapons are handled by his disciple Hajime.

58.content: Yae Publishing House is a giant of Inazuma's publishing industry, founded by Yae Miko, chief priestess of the Grand Narukami Shrine, who is also its editor-in-chief. It runs a contest named "This Novel Is Amazing!" and is famous across Teyvat. It publishes light literature, and the best-selling Liyue novel "A Legend of Sword" is serialised there.

59.content: A small detective agency in Hanamizaka, staffed by the detectives Ryuuji and Sango. Its board advertises investigation of missing persons, missing pets, marital questions, commercial commissions, procurement and delivery.

60.content:
Higi Village (also: Scarlet Tree Village): Higi Village is a small village on Yashiori Island in Inazuma, whose main export was Crystal Marrow. The war between the Watatsumi Army and the Shogun's Army, and then the Tatarigami curse of the serpent god Orobashi, emptied it. Most residents fled, died or were sacrificed; the chief Washizu, once a kind man, went mad, while a boy named Chouji tries to sell Crystal Marrow to leave.

The village's secret is grim: Washizu drew passing travellers into praying at his shrine, then tried to kill them as sacrifices to the voice in his head. The Traveler kills him in self-defence after several days of prayer. The pharmacist Yasumoto and the samurai Inaba Kyuuzou disappear along the way.

Geography: Higi lies on Yashiori Island in Inazuma. A Statue of the Seven stands on the northeastern side of the village, and the viewpoint for Serpent's Head, which lies southeast of the village, can be found inside it. The shrine at which Washizu keeps watch stands in the village, and Jakotsu Mine lies nearby.

Places: The village shrine, the chief's house, the pharmacist's house, Jakotsu Mine (where Chouji lives) and the central tree.

People: Washizu: village chief, now deranged. Yasumoto: pharmacist, student of the late Naoko. Chouji: a boy selling Crystal Marrow near Jakotsu Mine. Chouji's mother and father: both gone from the village.

Governance: Washizu governed as village chief with help from the village's pharmacists. Under the Shogunate, officers regularly visited to prevent the village from siding with the resistance and to take its Crystal Marrow, the main export, for the war.

Culture: Higi's way of life revolved around Crystal Marrow, a crystal containing a sliver of Tatarigami power that makes smelted metal stronger and tougher, and around shrines to quiet Orobashi's soul.

History: The village was one of the places worst hit by the Watatsumi Army-Shogun's Army war: constant losses, officers commandeering Crystal Marrow, refugees from Jakotsu Mine and a shortage of food. According to the wiki, when Orobashi fanatics in the Watatsumi Army broke the wards over Yashiori, the Tatarigami returned and the villagers fell sick or went mad. Many fled; some joined the pirates.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Higi Village remains largely abandoned; Washizu is dead and the curse has not been lifted.

Chouji has set out to find his parents, Yasumoto is missing and the chief is dead. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content revisits it.

61.comment: Higi Village: Washizu and the Outsider Shrine
61.content: Washizu was Higi Village's chief and a kind, welcoming man until the Tatarigami drove him mad. He took to praying at a shrine and urged strangers to join him, leaving rewards at their doorsteps. Over several days the Traveler prays with him, and on the last he tries to stab them, defeated in combat. His notes show he had been sacrificing villagers and passersby to a voice he calls "Him", using their belongings to lure others.

62.content: Chouji is a boy who lives near Jakotsu Mine. After the village emptied and his mother left, he began selling Crystal Marrow to travellers at inflated prices to earn the Mora to leave Yashiori and search for his parents. He is serious beyond his years, bargains sharply, and is wary of both Washizu and Yasumoto. The Traveler helps him mine; in return he teaches how to cook Imported Poultry and asks them to learn about his mother at the local shrines.

63.comment: Higi Village: The Tatarigami on Yashiori
63.content: The Tatarigami is the curse formed from the will and power of the serpent god Orobashi after Ei slew him on Yashiori Island, kept in check by wards. When the wards fail it causes thunderstorms, withering plants and untreatable illness. Victims suffer bleeding, fever, rashes, migraines, dizziness, hallucinated voices and madness, and Vision-holders are less affected.

64.content:
Inazuma (also: Nation of Eternity, Inazuma Archipelago, Land of Eternity): Inazuma is the island nation of Eternity off the far east of Teyvat, near the Dark Sea. Its god is the Electro Archon Raiden Ei, the Raiden Shogun. For centuries a deathless puppet (the Shogun) ruled in her place while her mind meditated in the Plane of Euthymia. The Shogunate governs from Inazuma City and the castle Tenshukaku on Narukami Island, with daily affairs run by the Tri-Commission. Inazuma is a land of cherry blossoms, red maples, thunderstorms, shrines, swordsmanship, and youkai living alongside humans. It was recently closed off by the Sakoku Decree, while the Vision Hunt Decree seized its people's Visions. Both decrees are now repealed.

Inazumans revere the Shogun as an unchanging god and have only recently begun to know Ei as a person. Watatsumi Island still worships its own slain god, Orobashi.

Geography: Inazuma has six main islands. Narukami holds the capital, the foreigners' port of Ritou and Mt. Yougou. Kannazuka has the Mikage Furnace. Yashiori is split by Musoujin Gorge. Watatsumi, with Sangonomiya Shrine, lies farthest from the capital. Seirai is storm-wracked and Tsurumi fog-bound. Enkanomiya lies under the sea beneath Watatsumi.

Government: The Raiden Shogun rules from Tenshukaku through the Tri-Commission. The Tenryou Commission (Kujou Clan) handles the military and security. The Kanjou Commission (Hiiragi Clan) handles finance and the borders. The Yashiro Commission (Kamisato Clan, under Kamisato Ayato) oversees shrines and festivals. The Grand Narukami Shrine under Guuji Yae Miko answers to the Archon, not to the Shogunate. Watatsumi is largely governed by its Divine Priestess, Sangonomiya Kokomi.

History: The twin gods Makoto and Ei won the archipelago in the Archon War. Their conquered youkai helped humans found a city by the sea, and Ei slew rival gods such as Orobashi more than 2,000 years ago. In the cataclysm 500 years ago Makoto died in Khaenri'ah. Fearing "erosion," Ei pursued Eternity: about 400 years ago she left the Shogun puppet to rule, sealed her mind in the Plane of Euthymia, and gave the Electro Gnosis to Yae Miko. A year before the Traveler came, the Fatui manipulated two commissions into the Sakoku and Vision Hunt decrees, which provoked a civil war with Watatsumi.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Inazuma is at peace and open. The Vision Hunt is over and the Visions have been returned, Sakoku is lifted, a ceasefire with Watatsumi holds, and Ei takes a more direct part in governing.

The Electro Gnosis is now in Fatui hands. The Archon Quest has since moved on to other nations, up to Snezhnaya (Chapter VII, 7.0-7.1). At the close of 7.1, after Ronova destroyed a Celestial Nail in Snezhnaya with Eitr, the other Nails across Teyvat began emitting pillars of light, and unusual activity was reported on Tsurumi Island, where a Nail is believed to have fallen. Yae Miko went to see for herself after drawing a "Great Misfortune" fortune slip; she senses a faint power there and means to bring Kokomi to look at it. What the phenomenon means is not yet known.

65.comment: Inazuma: The Tri-Commission and the Shogun's Army
