Dangers: Bandits and ronin, Treasure Hoarders and Kairagi linger in the wilder corners. Araumi's depths hold Ruin Guards and other ancient machines. Under Sakoku, foreigners trying to leave Ritou without a permit were turned back by its guards.

Travel: Ships from abroad dock at Ritou; it is the official way in. Roads link Ritou, Konda Village, Byakko Plain and Inazuma City, and boats cross to Kannazuka and the other islands.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Narukami Island is at peace. The Sakoku and Vision Hunt decrees are gone, foreigners move freely through Ritou, and Ei now takes a more active part in governing from Tenshukaku. No Narukami-specific story events appear in 6.x-7.1 content.

128.comment: Narukami Island: Konda Village and Byakko Plain
128.content: Konda Village, in the southwest of Narukami, has long been the Shogunate's main dye-producing village. It is simple, peaceful and known for Konda Cuisine, though Sakoku and the war aged it early. The road from Konda to Inazuma City crosses Byakko Plain, a low field where wild kitsune roam. Folk say a fox will not show itself twice to a traveler whose fate is not tied to its own.

129.content: Chinju Forest is a sacred grove just south of Mt. Yougou, on the path to the Kamisato Estate. For reasons nobody explains it lies under eternal night, lit by an unseen moon. Torii gates, tanuki statues and abandoned shrines fill it. Legend says demons once lived there, and rumour holds that pranksters still play tricks on those who walk through. The "tanuki-bayashi" tales of bake-danuki are tied to it.

130.content:
Nazuchi Beach (also: Nadzuchi no Hama): Nazuchi Beach is a stretch of shallow coast joining Kannazuka and Yashiori Island in Inazuma. Its name once meant "to be tenderly caressed by the hands of the gods", but the shoal has seen far too much battle. Torn flags, broken arrows, shattered masts and wrecked decks lie along it, and it has long been a haunt of scavengers, pirates and ronin. In the Archon Quest it is where the Sangonomiya Resistance faced the Shogun's Army.

During the Vision Hunt Decree war it was a front line between the Tenryou Commission and the Watatsumi Army, fought over by both land and sea. Few people live there; those who are met are mostly soldiers on missions, Treasure Hoarders and wanderers searching for lost things.

Geography: A shallow coastal strip joining Kannazuka and Yashiori Island, with a Teleport Waypoint in its western part and another in its northern part. Violet Ibis rest on the sand among the torn banners, arrows and wrecked ships. Dendrobium grows here, a rare flower for such a place.

People: The Shogunate soldiers Genzou and a superior, Terada, are on a mission near the waypoint; Genzou is the self-effacing subordinate, and Terada is evasive when asked what his mission is. The Treasure Hoarders Miura and Onoda scavenge the south, with Miura the bold boss and Onoda the nervous underling who fears running into either army; Miura's plan is to say they are with whoever they meet. Utsumi, a retired Shogunate soldier, searches an islet for his late son's belongings.

History: The beach has been a war zone for close to a thousand years, according to the in-game texts. In the Vision Hunt Decree conflict the Sangonomiya Resistance's front line was pushed back a couple of times until it settled at Nazuchi Beach, where fighting was chaotic and scattered forces could not tell friend from foe.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Pyro and Electro hilichurl shooters, Hydro slimes, Electro Whopperflowers, Nobushi and Kairagi, plus elites such as the Mirror Maiden and the Crackling Axe Mitachurl.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the beach remains a deserted battlefield of wrecks, stragglers and scavengers, with the Vision Hunt Decree war long over.

The decree was ended after the Archon Quest; no later canon through 7.1 changes the beach.

131.comment: Nazuchi Beach: Kannazuka and Fort Fujitou
131.content: Kannazuka ("the hill where no gods reside") is the rocky disputed territory beside the beach, claimed by neither the Shogunate nor Sangonomiya, where neither Inazuman nor Sangonomiya faith has influence. Mikage Furnace, Inazuma's largest smelting facility, which makes Jade Steel, lies there. General Gorou of the resistance is found at Fort Fujitou.

132.content:
Oina Beach (also: Oina Kaigan): Oina Beach is a subarea on the coast of Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. It has little recorded lore of its own, but in the world quest The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna the Traveler uses a Thunderbird feather on a Mysterious Carving here and sees part of Kanna Kapatcir's memories.

It is the second of three places, after Wakukau Shoal and before the Autake Plains, where the feather is used.

Geography: A stretch of shore on Tsurumi Island with Mysterious Carvings, Thunderstones, Thunder Barriers, Seelie and a Thunder Sakura Bough. Fluorescent Fungus grows here.

History: In the quest the feather draws out a vision from the Thunderbird's point of view: strange objects fell from the heavens and one landed on Tsurumi Island, after which her sky cleared and fog began to emerge. She had the power to disperse it and did not. The vision also shows the islanders gathering the feathers she shed at set intervals, a habit she found puzzling.

Quests: The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna (2.2). Ruin Cruiser and Ruin Destroyer must be defeated, then a Ruin Guard, before the feather memory is revealed. Ruu is not found here.

Dangers: Ruin Machines, hilichurls and Electro Abyss Mages; elites include Mitachurls.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no later canon read for this entry changes the beach.

133.content:
Outlander Affairs Agency (also: Ongoku Kansatsu, Outlander Affairs Bureau, Distant Country Supervision): The Outlander Affairs Agency is the Kanjou Commission office in Ritou that handles documents and requests from visitors who are not from Inazuma. While the Sakoku Decree was in force, any outsider who wanted to stay in Ritou had to apply here for a Residence Permit and pay a "handling fee", and the agency used its position to fleece stranded foreigners. Inspector Yurika runs the counter and Chiba guards the entrance.

The agency sits on the Kanjou Commission's watch over Inazuma's finances, customs and borders. Its reputation changed when the commission was purged of corruption: it grew more lenient and later quoted a modest official fee.

Geography: The agency is a point of interest in Ritou, the port island that handles all foreign arrivals and departures. Yurika wanders its courtyard, Chiba stands by the entrance, and the merchant Robert paces on the stairs outside.

People: Yurika is the Inspector at the counter; Chiba, an officer of the Kanjou Commission, keeps the door; the merchant Robert is a recurring applicant. The wiki lists no other staff. The commission's head, Hiiragi Shinsuke, stood above them until his arrest, after which his daughter Hiiragi Chisato became acting head of the clan.

Governance: The agency answers to the Kanjou Commission, the branch of the Tri-Commission responsible for Inazuma's wealth and borders. Rules for foreigners in Ritou were set by the Kanjou Commission's administration. Thoma tells the Traveler that to everyday Inazumans anyone from elsewhere is an "outsider" and that outlanders are unwelcome while the Sakoku Decree stands, even in the Outsider Settlement on Ritou.

History: When the Sakoku Decree left outsiders stranded on Ritou, the agency took advantage. In Confessions of an Outlander (2.0), Yurika asked the Traveler and Paimon for a processing fee of one million Mora each, two million in all. Out of courtesy to Thoma she cut it to 400,000 Mora, and Thoma then offered 600 Mora and dinner, which she accepted and recorded. The quest sets this in the Archon Quest scene where the Traveler registers at the border and the agency.

Quests: Confessions of an Outlander (Archon Quest, Chapter II Act I: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia, 2.0) sends the Traveler through the agency with Thoma. The agency is otherwise an ordinary map location with NPCs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the agency still exists in Ritou. Yurika and Chiba were last seen at their posts after the Sakoku Decree ended, and processing has become routine. No content from 5.x to 7.1 mentions the agency.

134.comment: Outlander Affairs Agency: Yurika's handling fee
134.content: Yurika quotes fees according to urgency: the more important an applicant's business, the higher the "handling fee" should be. During the Decree she demanded a Residence Permit application, an Entry Permit and unnamed "materials". After Omnipresence Over Mortals she says the fee is the official 500 Mora per visitor and invites doubters to check the Kanjou Commission's latest regulations. After the Decree ends she asks merchants for an Entry Permit and identification papers.

135.content: Robert, a merchant, travelled with a fleet and had a Snezhnayan friend help with his application, yet Yurika kept telling him he was missing "materials". He asks the Traveler what else he needs. After the Decree ends he muses about opening a shop in Ritou.

136.comment: Outlander Affairs Agency: Irodori Festival at the agency
136.content: During the limited Irodori Festival event (Hues of the Violet Garden), Yurika says guests may sign up at the agency to set up a fan-work booth and may certify family members to arrange their food and board; usual store and residency permits are still processed, with the handling fee reminder. Chiba urges visitors to stay mindful of their safety, and Robert says he wants to invite Ryouko to the festival. This is event-only dialogue.

137.content:
Outsider Shrine: The Outsider Shrine is a modest shrine at Serpent's Head on Yashiori Island, next to a man called Washizu. He insists that people who pray there three times in a day will be rewarded by a "he" who listens, and the shrine itself shows no sign of anything unusual. It is the centre of the hidden objective Washizu's Prayers.

The objective plays out over four real days. Washizu was once the kind chief of Higi Village; the Tatarigami outbreak on the island unmoored him, and the shrine is where his worship turned dangerous.

Geography: It stands at Serpent's Head, the bone-strewn coast of Yashiori Island, where Orobashi's remains lie. Flavour text for the prayers mentions sea breeze, gulls, distant whales, fireflies, wildflowers and wind through the great serpent's bones, as if weathered into the saddest instrument of the sea.

Quests: Washizu's Prayers (requires having done Ritou Escape Plan) is time-gated: pray daily for three days, then speak to Washizu on the fourth. His talk grows more feverish: the "words of the heart" over the "words of the tongue", a woman who refused tribute and fled, and a growing sense that "he" is angry. On the last day he attacks the Traveler as a maddened samurai and is defeated, which opens the hidden world quest Sinister Instruction in Higi Village.

Dangers: The shrine itself is harmless. Washizu is hostile only on the final day of the objective, and the following quest touches on human sacrifice (kept off-page here).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the objective and follow-up quest are unchanged, Washizu is dead, and the shrine's prayers no longer function after completion.

138.content:
Palace in a Pool: Palace in a Pool is a one-time domain beneath Suigetsu Pool on Watatsumi Island, Inazuma. Its description says that seawater once did not fill the pool and that moonlight, brighter then, flowed through it like quicksilver. It holds the ancient mansion of Umigozen, famed throughout Inazuma for a window where one could drink wine and watch the flowers; now it is empty and only bandits and thieves dwell there.

It has a single level, Tutelage: Umigozen's Mansion, and was added in Version 2.1.

Geography: Reached by draining part of Suigetsu Pool: Electro monuments are unlocked by using an Electrogranum on four probes, then the player dives through an opening toward a root, climbs it, opens a door by switches and drains the rest of the water.

Dangers: Nobushi: Hitsukeban, a Mirror Maiden, a Treasure Hoarder Pugilist and Cryo and Pyro Potioneers.

139.content:
Plane of Euthymia (also: Euthymia, Pure Land of One Mind, Isshin Joudo, Ei's inner world): The Plane of Euthymia is the inner world of Ei, the Raiden Shogun. Over 400 years ago, after building the Shogun puppet to rule in her place, Ei withdrew her consciousness into it to meditate on eternity and protect her spirit from decay. It is a space of mind, not a place one walks to, and it lies within the sword Musou Isshin kept inside the Shogun. For centuries Ei admitted no one.

The Traveler was drawn in three times: first as an "exception" to be judged, then to shake Ei's resolve with the light of the confiscated Visions, and later to persuade her to leave and see modern Inazuma. In Chinese the name is Yixin Jingtu, "Pure Land of One Mind".

Geography: It has no map as such. In the first judgment the Traveler finds bare gravel ground with torii rising from it in a dark void. Later it appears as a quiet, dark-skied space where Ei meditates, with Ei standing some distance away. It reflects her inner world, so its look follows her state of mind.

People: Ei is the only permanent occupant. The Shogun puppet does not live there, though she can confront Ei in consciousness-spaces. Outsiders enter only because Ei pulls them in or, on the Traveler's second visit, because Yae Miko appears through the Grand Narukami Shrine omamori she had given them.

History: Yae Miko once taught Ei how to place consciousness in objects. Ei used this to create the Plane and set it in the blade Musou Isshin, a sword made from her sister Makoto's divine might that passed to Ei after Makoto died in the cataclysm about 500 years ago. Over 400 years ago she retired into it, leaving the Shogun to pursue Inazuma's eternity. She could watch the world and take over the puppet at will, but cared only about matters touching eternity, which is why she tacitly accepted the Vision Hunt Decree.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Plane remains Ei's inner retreat, but she is no longer sealed in it.

Ei has ended the Vision Hunt Decree, and spends time in the outside world. No Plane of Euthymia content was found for the 6.x Nod-Krai or 7.0-7.1 releases.

140.content: The legendary sword made from Makoto's divine might. In her hands it was kept unsharpened as a symbol of true peace; after her death Ei took it into battle. Ei placed the Plane of Euthymia inside it, and the Shogun summons it from her chest. Makoto left a faint trace of her will in it, which was released after Ei's change of heart.

141.comment: Plane of Euthymia: The Vision Hunt Ceremony Trial
141.content: At the ceremony marking the 100th seized Vision, held at the Statue of the Omnipresent God, Thoma was to lose his. The Traveler intervened, was marked as an enemy of eternity and drawn into the Plane. In the fight the Shogun invoked the decree to stop other characters' Elemental Skills and Bursts, then delivered divine punishment. Thoma escaped with the unconscious Traveler.

142.comment: Plane of Euthymia: Ei's Lonesome Retreat
142.content: Ei had the Shogun disabled in part while she thought about Inazuma's eternity. The Traveler and Paimon persuaded her to tour Inazuma. The scene shows she is lonely in the Plane but sees her isolation as necessary.

143.content:
Police Station (also: Inazuma City Police Station, Bugyou-sho, Commissioner's Office): The Police Station is the Inazuma City office of the police, in the Tenryou district. Its in-game description says it is responsible for maintaining law and order in Inazuma, and the Japanese name means Commissioner's Office. It is staffed by the yoriki Owada, who just wants a quiet career, and a new doushin, Uesugi, who wants bigger cases.

Day-to-day the station takes reports from neighbours, which are mostly minor troubles and clumsy mistakes. It is a place for citizens to report anything out of order or any suspicious outsider, and a notice outside urges everyone to stay alert after hostile people were seen in Inazuma City.

Places: The office sits in Tenryou, the commercial district below Tenshukaku. Both officers wear the standard ashigaru-style uniform of the Inazuma Shogunate: purple-grey underclothes, eggplant-coloured armour with the Shogunate crest, and a cross-shaped spear. The notice board outside carries a public safety notice about hostile people in the city.

People: Owada, the yoriki, is superior to every doushin there. He describes himself as getting too old, hoping only to clock out on time and retire in peace, and insists he is not slacking: he has seen everything in his long career and simply wants a peaceful world. He prays each day that nothing eventful happens, and refers pet-loss cases to Ryuuji. Uesugi, the doushin, is a recent recruit who greets visitors with a cheer for the Shogun and her everlasting reign and wishes the job gave him a big case worth his skill.

Governance: The station is part of Inazuma's law-and-order machinery under the Shogunate; Owada and Uesugi swear by the Shogun and the Electro Archon, and doushin answer to the yoriki. The link to the Tenryou Commission, which the Kujou clan leads, is implied by Rikuto's remarks below rather than stated by the officers.

History: No founding history is given. Within the game's story the station appears during the period of the Sakoku Decree and the Vision Hunt Decree, when the city is on guard against outsiders.

Atmosphere: Quiet, stiff and a little sleepy. Owada startles easily and hopes nobody has come to report anything; Uesugi is eager and slightly bored. Behind the calm there is a sense that officials are anxious about outsiders and that the world outside is getting complicated.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the wiki records no change to the station: Owada and Uesugi are still listed as its staff and the notice text is the same.

144.content: Owada is the yoriki at the Police Station, an older officer who wants peace and a calm retirement rather than excitement. He prays that the Electro Archon will bless everyone, treats frequent reports with alarm, and recommends the Bantan Sango Detective Agency for lost pets. He is an old acquaintance of Ryuuji and regrets he could not help him when Ryuuji was framed.

145.content: Uesugi is a new doushin, eager for important cases and mildly horrified at the thought of ending up like Owada. He sometimes helps Ryuuji with cases, takes missing-family reports (including the Traveler's), and tells the story of Arataki Itto's planned sumo rematch with Kujou Sara.

146.content:
Ritou (also: Ritou Harbor, Outlying Island): Ritou is the port on Narukami Island where every non-Inazuman entering or leaving Inazuma is processed. It is under the jurisdiction of the Kanjou Commission, whose ruling Hiiragi Clan has its estate here, and it holds the Outlander Affairs Agency, the foreign merchants' International Trade Association, and a plaza shaded by a great red maple. Under the Sakoku Decree, foreigners who arrived could go no further without a hard-won Travel Permit.

Legend says Lord Hiiragi Hiroshi of the Kanjou Commission built it centuries ago from a deserted island into a thriving trade centre, greatly impressing the Shogun. The Traveler arrived here at the start of the Inazuma Archon Quest (2.0).

Geography: Ritou sits on a peninsula of Narukami Island, its name meaning "outlying island", with the docks at its entrance, a central area around the plaza, the Hiiragi Estate, a southern coast, and a guarded exit on the road toward the rest of Narukami. The official map describes a fishing village of red maples and green roof tiles. A Statue of The Seven stands near the shore.

Places: The docks, with Kanjou inspectors and the harbour bulletin board; the Outlander Affairs Agency, which handles foreigners' documents; the International Trade Association; the Hiiragi Estate, which serves as the Kanjou Commissioner's office; and the central plaza with its large maple, known since the Irodori Festival as the Five Kasen Plaza.

People: Kanjou Commission officers, inspectors and ashigaru; Hiiragi Chisato, acting head of the Hiiragi Clan; and a community of foreign merchants and sailors from Mondstadt, Liyue, Snezhnaya, Sumeru and elsewhere. Kurisu, born Christopher in Fontaine, founded and leads the International Trade Association and has helped many newcomers.

Governance: The Kanjou Commission, one of the Tri-Commission, manages Inazuma's finances, customs and borders from Ritou. Under the Sakoku Decree it ran a strict and corrupt regime: complicated assessments for entry or exit, heavy fees, and harsh treatment of foreigners. Commissioner Hiiragi Shinsuke conspired with the Fatui and was arrested after the 2.1 Archon Quest; his daughter Chisato now acts as clan head, and the commission has treated foreigners far better since.

History: Lord Hiiragi Hiroshi wanted foreign trade centralised under the government and built Ritou to do it. To prove its worth he imported foreign inventions, among them a Snezhnayan blast furnace used to create the hot springs at Tenshukaku as a gift for the Shogun. When the Sakoku Decree sealed Inazuma about a year before the Traveler arrived, storms ringed the islands and foreign merchants were stranded in Ritou; the official viewpoint says the streets lost the bustle of a century before while the Kanjou Commission itself still flourished.

Atmosphere: Red maples, green tiles, the creak of the docks and a mix of accents. Under Sakoku it felt like a waiting room: outlanders idling in the plaza, staring out at the empty sea, short of money and patience. Since the decree ended it has been busier, though still the place where foreigners first deal with Inazuman paperwork.

Quests: Chapter II Act I (2.0): Setting Sail, Confessions of an Outlander and Ritou Escape Plan, followed by the world quest Chisato's Letter, which earns the Travel Permit. Kamisato Ayato's story quest (2.6) involves a plot inside the Hiiragi Clan. The 2.6 event Hues of the Violet Garden takes place here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Ritou is open: the Sakoku Decree was abolished in 2.5, foreigners come and go freely after processing, and the Kanjou Commission is far less corrupt under Hiiragi Chisato.

Hiiragi Shinsuke remains imprisoned. No new events in Ritou appear in the Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) storylines.

147.content: The Kanjou Commission's office for foreign visitors' documents and requests. Under the Sakoku Decree it fleeced stranded outlanders: the inspector Yurika first asked the Traveler for two million Mora, and Thoma talked her down to 600, saying such practices were common. After the commission was purged of corruption, the agency became more lenient and charges a processing fee of 500 Mora.

148.content: Founded by foreigners to trade in Inazuma (importing goods such as Silk Flowers) and to help newcomers survive the Kanjou Commission's harsh treatment. Its president Kurisu, a Fontainian who took an Inazuman name, welcomes outlanders in trouble. During the Irodori Festival it housed the foreign guests of honour, and the plaza in front of it was named the Five Kasen Plaza.

149.content: The Kanjou Commission suddenly demanded the association's taxes in Crystal Marrow rather than Mora. The officer Keijirou and his men bought up the supply and resold it through Werner, a former member from Mondstadt, at ever-higher prices. The Traveler found Keijirou's hidden ledger; when an officer, Katsuie, moved to arrest the merchants, Thoma produced a Yashiro Commission card and an ornate fan, and the matter was dropped. The Crystal Marrow the commission collected later turned out to feed the Fatui's Delusion factory.

150.comment: Ritou: Ritou Escape Plan and the Travel Permit
150.content: Barred from leaving Ritou, the Traveler visited Commissioner Hiiragi Shinsuke, who set absurd tasks (300 freshly picked Qingxin, or delivering 709 letters). His daughter Chisato secretly summoned them at night, revealed that an arrogant woman (Signora) had conspired with her father to keep them on Ritou, and slipped them out as the "qualified escort" for a Kanjou shipment she accompanied personally. Her letter to Kujou Kamaji of the Tenryou Commission in Inazuma City then earned them a Travel Permit to come and go freely.

151.content:
Royal Hot Springs (also: Royal Bath, Royal Bathhouse, Go-onsen, Imperial Onsen): The Royal Hot Springs is a hot-spring bathhouse at the headquarters of the Tenryou Commission in Inazuma City, near Tenshukaku. It is reserved for the lords of the Shogunate, who are served and housed by its manager Mikawa Akane, and outsiders are not allowed in.

Access is based on a strict hierarchy. With private rooms and very few customers, the springs are often used for the lords' private discussions. Inazuma has no natural volcanic hot springs, so the water is heated artificially and mixed with minerals and plants from many nations.

Places: The baths lie in the Tenshukaku part of Inazuma City, within the Tenryou Commission's headquarters. The Court Lantern "Thundering Heart" furnishing describes lanterns found in Tenshukaku and at the Royal Hot Springs, coated in a solution made from trace amounts of Amethyst Lumps and Electro Crystals, which makes them brighter and lightning-resistant.

People: Mikawa Akane greets visitors by naming the Royal Hot Springs and its location at the Tenryou Commission headquarters, and asks whether an unfamiliar visitor has got lost. She arranges service and rooms for Shogunate lords who come for the hot springs. She is happy to tell new arrivals about Inazuma's hot-spring culture, but refuses to let an outsider bathe.

Governance: The springs are for the Shogunate's lords, and the baths sit at the Tenryou Commission headquarters. Akane says access priority follows a strict hierarchy. The Kanjou Commission figure Hiiragi Hiroshi is credited with the first Inazuma hot spring, and Akane muses that a spring funded by that Commission could offer commoners the same benefits.

History: Hot-spring culture came to Inazuma from elsewhere, and the locals were enchanted by it. Having no volcanic springs, they tried many ways to make one. According to Akane, Hiiragi Hiroshi of the Kanjou Commission solved it with a Snezhnayan boiler, creating the first Inazuma hot spring.

Atmosphere: Quiet, formal and secluded: private rooms, very few customers and staff who know who may enter. The temperature of the water is, as Akane says, just right.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the springs are still reserved for Shogunate lords with Akane as manager; the wiki records no change since 2.0.

152.content: Mikawa Akane is the manager of the Royal Hot Springs. She is polite but firm, offers hot-spring history to newcomers, and refuses outsiders because the springs are for the Shogunate's lords by strict rank. She is irritated by Tae, a new employee who skips work.

153.comment: Royal Hot Springs: Tae, the Fatui Spy at the Baths
153.content: In the world quest "Shuumatsuban Operations" the Traveler is told one of three Fatui spies has recently started working at the Royal Hot Springs. Tae is a Fatui agent, disguised as staff, who dislikes Lyudochka Snezhevna, whom she accuses of getting the Grand Narukami Shrine post through luck. She is touchy, uses Fatui code phrases, and is suspected by the Tenryou Commission after the frostbite incident.

154.content:
Sacred Sakura (also: Shin'ou, Giant Thunder Sakura, Primeval Sakura, Crimson Sakura): The Sacred Sakura is the divine tree that towers over the Grand Narukami Shrine at the top of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island. It stands for the Electro Archon's protection of Inazuma: its roots purify the land's ley lines and keep Abyssal corruption from invading, and the sakura blossoms across the island have all fallen from it. Because filth builds up in its roots, the Grand Narukami Shrine must perform the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual from time to time.

Its offshoots, the Thunder Sakura, are found all over the land, and it is said that its protection reaches wherever its petals come to rest. The people of Inazuma remember it as having always been there, though its origin is stranger than that.

Geography: The tree rises over the Grand Narukami Shrine at the top of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island. Its roots spread under the whole land, and the Thunder Sakura grafted from its side branches are connected to the same single root system. Beside the mountain at its foot is a large pool of Electrified Water that drains health until the cleansing is done.

History: Inazuman tradition holds that the Sacred Sakura cleanses the land of impurity through the Thunder Sakura, defending earth and water alike. Records say the Thunder Sakura almost withered several hundred years ago, when monsters raged and the seas around Inazuma turned black; someone eventually performed the Cleansing Ritual and the crisis ended. The ritual has a minor form, done often to check the roots and set up protective barriers, and a major form needed every sixty years: first the Thunder Sakura roots are purified, then the central roots of the Sacred Sakura.

Quests: The Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual is a World Quest series that begins at Konda Village. The Traveler meets the masked shrine maiden Hanachirusato, lifts barriers with wards, clears the Thunder Sakura roots at Araumi, the Kamisato Estate and Chinju Forest, then breaks the barrier at the Depths of Mt. Yougou and purges the Miasmic Tumor there. Hanachirusato then reveals she is filth condensed from the memory of the Kitsune Saiguu, and must be cleansed with the rest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sacred Sakura is cleansed and glowing. No 6.x or 7.x content altering that was found on the wiki.

The story of the tree's origin is already told in the Raiden Shogun's Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter.

155.comment: Sacred Sakura: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual
155.content: The ritual keeps the connected roots of the Sacred Sakura and the Thunder Sakura clean. The Grand Narukami Shrine ordinarily performs it. Minor cleansings check the roots and raise barriers that protect the roots from malicious people such as the Fatui and protect the people from leaking filth. The major cleansing, due every 60 years, breaks those barriers with wards so the filth is driven out and condenses into forms: harmless ones such as the tofu-like figures in peaceful times, dangerous ones in times of strife. At the central roots the filth condenses into a Miasmic Tumor.

156.content: The Thunder Sakura are trees grafted from side branches of the Sacred Sakura; they absorb filth into their roots to purify the land. Their roots connect to the central tree's, so pollution spreads between them. Sakura Bloom, a local specialty of Narukami Island, comes from the Sacred Sakura.

157.content:
Sangonomiya Shrine (also: The Pearlescent Palace, Coral Palace): Sangonomiya Shrine, also called the Pearlescent Palace, stands at the centre of Watatsumi Island, the outermost island of Inazuma. A palace flanked by shells and sea rocks, it is the island's centre of government and religion alike: here the Divine Priestess Sangonomiya Kokomi rules, and here rest relics of Orobashi, the dead serpent god whom Watatsumi's people still worship instead of the Raiden Shogun. During the war against the Vision Hunt Decree it was the headquarters of the Watatsumi Army.

Its name means "Coral Palace". The island's shrine maidens are trained here. The present shrine is said not to be the island's original one, but a newer building raised after Orobashi was slain by the Electro Archon about 2,000 years ago.

Geography: The shrine lies in the middle of Watatsumi Island, ringed by mountains and waterfalls and surrounded by the island's strangely coloured, densely growing vegetation, with its violet-leaved forests. Bourou Village, the island's main settlement and the resistance's training camp, lies nearby, and Mouun Shrine stands elsewhere on the island. Sango Pearls and Sea Ganoderma are gathered in the surrounding area.

Places: The main palace-shrine, where Kokomi receives officers and guests; the shrine grounds, where Watatsumi soldiers keep watch; and nearby woods with a tree with purple foliage that Kokomi's written directives name as a landmark for finding her when she has slipped away.

People: Sangonomiya Kokomi, Divine Priestess and supreme leader of Watatsumi Island, lives and works here. General Gorou commands the island's army. Shrine maidens trained at the shrine include Izumi Naki, Mochizuki, Tsuyuko, Shizuru and Miwa; Sangonomiya samurai such as Shibata and Sugiyama stand guard, and officers such as Ookubo Daisuke report here on supplies.

Governance: The shrine is the seat of the Sangonomiya Clan, the only great Inazuman clan with no post in the Shogunate. The heir of their bloodline holds the title Divine Priestess, which means inheriting the will of a god in a mortal body and defending the land and people in that god's place. Kokomi handles war, trade, diplomacy and domestic affairs herself and governs through detailed written directives.

Culture: Watatsumi's people descend from Enkanomiya, a realm deep beneath the sea; Orobashi brought them to the surface, and they revere it as Watatsumi Omikami, their guardian god. Faith in the slain god, pride, and a long memory of defeat bind the community. The island keeps customs distinct from the capital's.

History: About 2,000 years ago, near the end of the Archon War, Orobashi raised Watatsumi Island from coral and led the people of Enkanomiya there. Hunger drove them to invade Yashiori Island; the Electro Archon struck back, and Orobashi was slain with the Musou no Hitotachi, which split Yashiori and left the Tatarigami behind. The old main shrine was abandoned and the present one built, with the Divine Priestess leading the island. When the Vision Hunt Decree came, the shrine became the resistance's headquarters.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter II, Act III "Omnipresence Over Mortals" (2.1): in "Sword, Fish, Resistance" Teppei brings the Traveler to the shrine, where Kokomi appoints them captain of the special operations unit Swordfish II; later the Traveler returns here and identifies the sponsor's weapons as Delusions. Kokomi's Story Quest (Dracaena Somnolenta Chapter) starts near the shrine. The world quest series "The Moon-Bathed Deep" begins when Tsuyuko, a shrine maiden of Sangonomiya Shrine, approaches the Traveler at Mouun Shrine; the entrance to Enkanomiya she describes is the deep pool directly across from Sangonomiya Shrine.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine is peaceful and still Kokomi's seat. The Vision Hunt Decree was abolished, peace talks with the Shogunate followed, and the Watatsumi Army now serves mainly as peacekeepers and helps rebuild.

Talks on bringing the island back under direct Shogunate rule made progress but were paused after the Fatui's meddling in the war came to light, so the island kept its army. Some residents still find peace with the Shogunate hard to accept. No 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story shown involves the shrine.

158.comment: Sangonomiya Shrine: Divine Priestess of Watatsumi
158.content: The Divine Priestess is the hereditary head of the Sangonomiya Clan and supreme leader of Watatsumi Island, ruling from Sangonomiya Shrine. The title means carrying a god's will in a mortal body and protecting the island and people in Orobashi's place. The current holder, Sangonomiya Kokomi, would rather have been a strategist working behind the scenes, but took up the role and is deeply loved by her people. Soldiers and islanders call her "Her Excellency".

159.comment: Sangonomiya Shrine: Orobashi's relics at the shrine
159.content: The viewpoint text calls the shrine the place where the relics of the serpent god lie. Orobashi, called Watatsumi Omikami, once ruled in Enkanomiya, taught its people to farm and smelt, and raised Watatsumi Island from its own coral before dying at the Electro Archon's hand. Its bones lie on Yashiori Island and its resentment became the Tatarigami. The shrine remains the heart of its worship.

160.content:
Seirai Island: Seirai Island is a broken, storm-wracked island of Inazuma. About 1,500 years ago the Thunderbird, Kanna Kapatcir, ravaged it until the Electro Archon killed her on Amakumo Peak, and wards held back the storm her death left. About 500 years ago a shrine maiden broke those wards to help the pirate Ako Domeki rebel against the Shogunate. A huge Electro storm then engulfed the island's centre, shattered the land and drove its people away for good. Today only Asase Shrine stands intact, kept by a talking cat called Neko who still waits for her mistress to return.

The Traveler recently resealed the storm with the help of two Adventurers' Guild members.

Geography: Seirai is a cluster of fragmented landmasses around a central basin. Until recently a perpetual thunderstorm filled that basin, with Balethunder and lightning striking anyone who entered. Amakumo Peak rises inland above a lake, with flooded underground ruins below it. Koseki Village, the abandoned fishing village, lies on the coast, as do the wreck of the flagship Seiraimaru and the ruins of Fort Hiraumi. Asase Shrine sits apart with fair weather of its own.

Places: - **Asase Shrine**: built to manage the wards over the Thunderbird's lingering hatred; the only place the storm left untouched.
- **Koseki Village**: the island's former fishing village, now silent; its people helped keep the shrine and made offerings there.
- **Amakumo Peak**: where Ei slew Kanna Kapatcir and where the Thunder Manifestation later appeared.
- **"Seiraimaru"**: the stranded wreck of Ako Domeki's flagship.
- **Fort Hiraumi**: ruins of the city of Hiraumi, destroyed by the Thunderbird.

People: Since the evacuation Seirai has no settled human population. Neko, a cat who can speak and no longer ages, calls herself the shrine's "Provisional Head Priestess" and watches over generations of shrine cats. The cats are named after "good things", and the names pass down the generations. The Adventurers' Guild members Etsuko and Taisuke stay at the shrine after the storm ends.

History: Seirai is thought to be one of the few islands that survived the great flood after the war of funerary flame. About 1,500 years ago, after destroying the tribe on Tsurumi Island, Kanna Kapatcir came to Seirai, wrecked much of it and left the city of Hiraumi in ruins. To protect her people, Ei hunted and killed the Thunderbird on Amakumo Peak. Warding Stones held back the storm left by her death, and the Asase Clan's shrine maintained the wards. About 500 years ago, a few years after the cataclysm, the pirate captain Ako Domeki led Seirai in rebellion against the Shogunate. Asase Hibiki, the shrine's head priestess, unsealed the wards with magic she had learned from the Yougou Tengu to destroy the Shogunate's ships. The storm that followed tore the island apart. The Shogunate evacuated the islanders to Narukami Island, and Hibiki never came back from the storm.

Atmosphere: Rain-black skies, fractured cliffs and abandoned houses, with the thunder only recently stilled. The Koseki Village viewpoint says the old laughter and cicada song have been lost to the thunder, and people now only remember that the place was abandoned to the storms. Asase Shrine, by contrast, is bright, tidy and full of cats.

Dangers: Before the Traveler resealed the Warding Stones, Balethunder and targeted lightning made the centre deadly. The Thunder Manifestation, a coagulation of the Thunderbird's regret, still appears there (gameplay: a repeatable boss on a platform formed above the island). Ruin Sentinels and slimes haunt the flooded ruins under Amakumo Peak.

Quests: In Seirai Stormchasers (2.1), sent by Katheryne, the Traveler joins the adventurers Etsuko and Taisuke. With Neko's guidance they reseal the four Warding Stones and defeat the Thunder Manifestation, which ends the storm. The Traveler also finds a Peculiar Pinion, a Thunderbird feather that matters later on Tsurumi Island. In Neko Is a Cat, the Traveler restores Asase Shrine for Neko.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the storm is sealed but the island stays depopulated, with only adventurers passing through and Neko tending Asase Shrine. She still believes Hibiki, Domeki and Janome will come back. No Seirai-specific story content appears in 6.x-7.1.

161.comment: Seirai Island: Asase Shrine and Neko
161.content: Asase Shrine on Seirai Island was founded after Kanna Kapatcir's death to manage the wards over her lingering hatred, and the Asase Clan ran it. Five centuries ago its head priestess Asase Hibiki broke the wards, but the shrine itself was spared by the storm. Neko, the cat Hibiki named, somehow stopped ageing, learned to speak, and has kept the shrine ever since, calling herself its "Provisional Head Priestess". She does not know that the islanders were evacuated, or that Hibiki must have died long ago, and she hopes a restored shrine will bring visitors and Hibiki back.

162.content:
"Seiraimaru" (also: Seiraimaru, The Stranded Flagship): "Seiraimaru" is a subarea of Seirai Island named for the flagship of the bandit captain Ako Domeki, which was destroyed there. The rundown atakebune warship lies stranded among thunder-scarred terrain, its wreck still marked by what looks like starlit tears.

The viewpoint text recalls a vessel that once sailed proudly, blessed by the shrine maidens and villagers of a bygone age.

History: Ako Domeki, called the Deathless Oni of Seirai, was a famed bandit and pirate from Seirai Island who led a rebellion against the Shogunate around 500 years ago and commanded over ten ships. The Seiraimaru was his flagship. The Shogunate's ships, and the island itself, were wrecked when Asase Hibiki unsealed the Thunder Manifestation to help his cause; the storm swept Ako and his crew away.

Quests: Exploring the ship is a multi-stage puzzle. Four wheels by the mast must be turned so single-pointed "sword" marks face three-pointed "halberd" marks, opening a hatch into the hull. Seelie guide the way inside: a Rust-Worn Key and wheel puzzle unlock an Exquisite Chest, and an Intact Key does the same for a Luxurious Chest (and the Davy Jones' Locker achievement) before another Seelie Court.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ship remains a wreck on Seirai Island, nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes it.

163.content:
Serpent's Head (also: Serpent Head, Orobashi's skull): The Serpent's Head is the skull of the great serpent god Orobashi, the Watatsumi Omikami, left on Yashiori Island where the Electro Archon killed it. The weathered bones now form a landscape of their own: a subarea of Inazuma battered by rain and thunder. The skull still gazes at the sky, but the god is dead and its name is slowly being forgotten.

The Tatarigami left by the god's remains drove the island's people away. The sea wind through the skull's eyes and fangs is said to make a whistling sound, called the requiem the serpent composed for itself.

Geography: The Serpent's Head is a subarea of Yashiori Island, the bony remains of Orobashi's skull rising over the sea and surrounded by thunderstorms. A viewpoint, Overlooking Serpent Head, looks over it. Inside the serpent's mouth a closed grate blocks the way down to a Simple Tomb under the skull, which is opened by a short puzzle: chase two Electro Seelies to the serpent's eyes, pull a lever beside a Thunder Sakura Bough in the first chamber, defeat a Ruin Sentinel in the second and trip the door switches in order. In the bottom chamber lies Kikuchiyo's Simple Tomb, guarded by a Kairagi.

History: After the Raiden Shogun and her twin Makoto united Inazuma, the other gods did not claim land that was not theirs. Orobashi, god of the Watatsumi people, was among them. Its island home was poor soil, and between the cries of its starving people and a decree from Celestia it invaded resource-rich Yashiori Island with a navy led by the shrine maiden Mouun and her sister Ayame. Ei gathered her troops and waged a brutal war, and slew Orobashi with Musou no Hitotachi, the blow splitting the island into two with Musoujin Gorge and leaving the god's remains across the land. The god's lingering hatred became the Tatarigami, which Ei suppressed with wards.

Quests: In Orobashi's Legacy the Traveler meets Kaji at Fort Fujitou, who is investigating the island's endless rain and lightning and traces it to broken ancient wards. One of the early parts (I to III) has the Traveler find missing Rock Pillar Warding Stones and Pearls and return them to the ward at the Serpent's Head, solving Sacred Stone Puzzles, as is also done at Musoujin Gorge and Jakotsu Mine. After the three wards are mended, Fort Mumei rises from the sea and the final, larger ward is repaired in Parts IV and V; the permanent rain and storm then cease.

Dangers: Constant rain and lightning until Orobashi's Legacy is completed, which applies Wet and can chain into Electro-Charged; Tatarigami influence; Maguu Kenki; Nobushi, Kairagi and Treasure Hoarders.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Serpent's Head remains a desolate, largely deserted site; the storms cease once Orobashi's Legacy is completed.

No 6.x or 7.x events concerning it were found on the wiki. The Fatui who lingered on Yashiori after the war are few.

164.content: Ei's wards, tied to Narukami Pillars, suppressed the Tatarigami for centuries, but a group of Watatsumi radicals destroyed them. In Orobashi's Legacy, the Traveler, working with Kaji's investigation, mends them by returning Warding Stones and Pearls. Each repair clears the Tatarigami over its own area; the Serpent's Head, Musoujin Gorge and Jakotsu Mine come first, then Fort Mumei's ward.

165.content: Beneath the skull lies Kikuchiyo's Simple Tomb, one of the Simple Tombs on Yashiori Island, reached through the grate in the serpent's mouth.

166.content:
Shakkei Pavilion (also: Tutelage: Castle of Scrolls): Shakkei Pavilion is a one-time domain in Tatarasuna, Kannazuka, Inazuma. Its description says the magnificent mansion was built by an ancient ascetic warrior in the depths of the earth, using scenery borrowed from the outside world (shakkei, a garden-design principle), and was sealed at some point for reasons unknown.

It has a single level, Tutelage: Castle of Scrolls, and was added in Version 2.0. The entrance is hidden behind rocks that must be broken by firing a Kamuijima Cannon.

Geography: Deep within Tatarasuna's rocky mountains, a mansion of brittle floors (broken by plunging attacks), amulet shrines and a main door that opens when three amulets are placed.

Dangers: Nobushi: Jintouban and Hitsukeban guard the shrines; the final room holds a Fatui Pyro Agent and a Mirror Maiden.

History: Before Version 3.3 the domain's description ended: 'In latter days, a deeply disheartened eccentric would be discovered within.' The wiki reads this as a veiled reference to the Wanderer (Scaramouche), called a kabukimono (eccentric) in Tatarasuna.

167.content:
Shirikoro Peak (also: Shirikoro-yama, Shirikoro Mountain): Shirikoro Peak is a rugged part of Tsurumi Island, the fog-shrouded island of Inazuma that once held two ancient civilisations. A great tree called a perch stands in a cave here, one of the places where the islanders once made offerings to the Thunderbird. Beneath the peak runs a stretch of underground ruins full of Electro puzzles, Seelie courts and ancient Ruin machines.

It is one of several perch sites (with Chirai Shrine, Autake Plains and the first perch) in the world quest series Through the Mists, where the Traveler helps the spirit of a boy named Ruu break a curse laid on the island by the Thunderbird. The name is Japanese Shirikoro-yama; "shirikoro" may come from the Ainu for "owning land".

Geography: The peak lies on Tsurumi Island, and its perch is inside a cave reached from the southeast, with three Seelie Courts nearby. Features of the peak include Mysterious Carvings, Phase Gates, Ruins Torches, Thunder Barriers and Thunder Sakura boughs. Local specialties are Fluorescent Fungus and Sea Ganoderma.

Places: The perch cave. A broken dome holding a remarkable chest. Doors of the buried ruin that open when Electro Current puzzles are solved. Seelie courts around a central mechanism.

History: Tsurumi Island is the home of two ancient peoples: an older civilisation buried deep underground, and later the tribe that worshipped the Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir. The perches were trees where the Thunderbird once alighted, and the islanders believed offerings to them were needed. The story that unfolds in the quests: Ruu, child of the last priest Mata, befriended the Thunderbird by singing and named her Kanna Kapatcir; when the island declined he was chosen as a living sacrifice, which enraged her and she destroyed the village and cursed the island to relive its ruin.

Dangers: Hilichurl Fighters and Shooters, Samachurls, Electro Whopperflowers, and elites: Electro Abyss Mages, Wooden Shieldwall Mitachurls, Thundercraven Rifthound Whelps and several Ruin machines. The fog of Tsurumi Island teleports travellers away until cleared by the quests.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tsurumi Island's fog is gone and the curse is lifted, so the peak is a quiet ruin-filled hill.

Ruu is expected to pass on. No later canon through 7.1 changes the peak.

168.comment: Shirikoro Peak: Through the Mists and the Perches
168.content: In A Particularly Particular Author, the author Sumida, whose commission is posted through the Adventurers' Guild, asks the Traveler to fetch a Maushiro from Tsurumi Island for her novel; Kama takes them across by boat, and the Bantan Sango Detective Agency also takes an interest. The Traveler meets a boy, Ruu, and helps make offerings to perches, including the one at Shirikoro Peak. The locals behave oddly because they are illusions replaying the past. The Maushiro is gone when delivered, as for every adventurer before. The series continues in Octave of the Maushiro, and ends with the curse lifted and the island's fog permanently cleared.

169.content:
Slumbering Court: Slumbering Court is a Domain of Blessing at Fort Hiraumi on Seirai Island, Inazuma. Its description says this great hall stood when Seirai Island had neither its present name nor the colour of thunder, and that the scenery within will probably never change. The masterless mansion has become a haunt of rifthounds.

Clearing it yields artifacts: Husk of Opulent Dreams, Ocean-Hued Clam, Defender's Will and Brave Heart. It was added in Version 2.3.

Geography: A great hall in the Fort Hiraumi area of Seirai Island, the island of the perpetual thunderstorm.

Dangers: Hydro slimes and a Crackling Axe Mitachurl at the lower levels, then Thundercraven Rifthound whelps and Rifthounds at the higher ones, with Electro Hilichurl Shooters.

key: Statue of the Thousand-Armed, Hundred-Eyed God
170.content:
Statue of the Omnipresent God (also: Statue of the Thousand-Armed, Hundred-Eyed God, Symbol of Eternity, Shogun's statue): The Statue of the Omnipresent God is a vast statue built in front of Tenshukaku in Inazuma City as the "Symbol of Eternity". It was raised after the Vision Hunt Decree so that every confiscated Vision could be embedded in it. Its Visions were taken away and returned to their owners after the Traveler defeated Ei in Chapter II. Its earlier English name was the Statue of the Thousand-Armed, Hundred-Eyed God.

Ninety-nine Visions had been seized by the time of Amidst Stormy Judgment. Who the statue shows is never stated: many Inazumans simply call it the Shogun's statue.

Geography: It stands before Tenshukaku, the Raiden Shogun's residence on Narukami Island,. Visions are inlaid across its body, including Arataki Itto's, set near the bottom just above a Pyro Vision whose owner is unknown. After Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow, a Patrol Soldier stops anyone approaching it.

History: The Vision Hunt Decree was issued by the Raiden Shogun and the Shogunate about a year before the story, to seize Visions across Inazuma and inlay them in the statue; the Tenryou Commission carried it out. It began as a Fatui plot to cause unrest and create a market for Delusions; Kujou Takayuki agreed to help in exchange for their promises of support, and deceived the Shogun into continuing it. Ei, the true Shogun, knew of the Fatui involvement but approved, believing individual ambition would only lead to loss and suffering and was incompatible with her ideal of eternity. The Traveler challenged Ei in her realm by showing her the power of the seized Visions' aspirations, and Ei repealed the decree. The Visions were removed from the statue and returned to their owners.

Quests: Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow (Chapter II, Act II) is the quest in which the Vision Hunt Ceremony is the reason the decree is being carried out. In The Omnipresent God (Chapter II, Act III) and the quest Omnipresence Over Mortals, the Traveler defeats Ei and the Visions are returned to their rightful owners.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the statue's Visions are gone: they were returned to their owners after Chapter II. The decree was repealed.

Its identity remains debated, and no 6.x or 7.x content on the wiki changes this.

171.comment: Statue of the Omnipresent God: Vision Hunt Decree
171.content: The decree ordered all Visions in Inazuma seized and inlaid in the Statue of the Omnipresent God. The Tenryou Commission enforced it. People who objected hid Visions or made decoys; many joined the Watatsumi Army. The decree is repealed in Chapter II, and the Visions are returned.

172.content:
Suigetsu Pool (also: Suigetsu-chi, Water-Moon Pool): Suigetsu Pool, the "Water-Moon Pool", is a subarea of Watatsumi Island in Inazuma. A once-famous mansion belonging to the warrior Umigozen lies beneath it, and the place is covered with ancient ruins and Ruin Machines. The mansion is the setting of the one-time domain Palace in a Pool.

The domain's lore text says that long ago seawater had yet to fill the pool and moonlight filled it instead, flowing like quicksilver.

Geography: A sunken pool and a ruin-strewn stretch of Watatsumi Island, with a hole leading down to the mansion. Electro Seelie, Electro Current puzzles, Thunder Sakura Boughs, Lightning Strike Probes, Thunder Dwellings and a Waverider Waypoint are found here. Sango Pearl and Sea Ganoderma are local specialties.

Places: Umigozen's Mansion (Palace in a Pool, the single level "Tutelage: Umigozen's Mansion"): once a grand house with a window for drinking wine and watching blossoms, now empty except for bandits, Nobushi and Treasure Hoarders, with sliding doors that hide amulets needed to open the last gate.

People: Umigozen is Yuna Ayame, a diver of the Yuna Clan of Watatsumi Island who lived about 2,000 years ago and was one of the leaders of the Watatsumi forces in the Narukami-Watatsumi War. Her older twin sister was the shrine maiden Mouun. She was the first owner of the weapon Wavebreaker's Fin and disappeared into the ocean at the war's end.

History: After the war the mansion stood abandoned; seawater covered it and its entrance was sealed. Today the only occupants are criminals using the place as a hideout.

Dangers: Treasure Hoarders (Pugilists and Potioneers), Nobushi including a Mirror Maiden, and ancient Ruin Machines.

Quests: No world quest is set here in the pages read; the Palace in a Pool domain is the main attraction, and a torn page of the Toki Alley Tales storybook can be found in the ruins.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the mansion remains abandoned; no later canon read for this entry changes it.

173.content:
Tatarasuna (also: Tatara Sands): Tatarasuna is an island in Kannazuka, Inazuma, ringed by mountainous crags with a huge blast furnace, the Mikage Furnace, at its centre. It was where Inazuma smelted its famed Jade Steel, powered by Tatarigami energy. Twice it has gone wrong: about 400 years ago in the incident remembered as the Tatarasuna Mystery, and again in the war years when the furnace's runaway power and Fatui interest in it brought the Traveler to help. Today the furnace is purified and the area is quiet.

Its Japanese name is Tatara-suna, echoing the tatara, the traditional Japanese smelting furnace. In the Traveler's day the furnace sits inside a containment dome and its surroundings are tainted by Balethunder, until the Tatara Tales quest series settles it.

Geography: A rough island of jagged, mountainous crags enclosing a central depression where the Mikage Furnace stands. It belongs to Kannazuka, near Yashiori Island, whose Tatarigami energy fed the furnace. The ground is stony and wind-scoured, dotted with thunder sakura, electric currents, lightning-strike probes and old Kamuijima cannons.

Places: Mikage Furnace: the plant itself, the largest smelting facility in Inazuma's islands, built to produce Jade Steel in bulk. Shakkei Pavilion: a pavilion tied to the Mystery. Kamuijima cannons: three unused cannons on the eastern side, later fired to breach the containment dome.

People: Present day: Xavier, a Fontaine engineer who stayed behind to maintain the furnace; Toranosuke, a Shogunate soldier, and Miyuki, a shrine maiden, who quarrel over what to do about it; and Fatui agents who breached the dome. Four centuries ago: the Armory Officer Niwa Hisahide, Vice Armory Officer Miyazaki Kaneo, Inspector Mikoshi Nagamasa and his yoriki Katsuragi, plus Nozomu and Kinjirou of Nagamasa's entourage.

History: Tatarasuna and its furnace were built to smelt Jade Steel, and Dottore later claimed the site had first been established to dispose of Crystal Marrow safely. Around 400 years ago the Armory Officer Niwa Hisahide, Inspector Mikoshi Nagamasa and Nagamasa's yoriki Katsuragi befriended a young man they called the kabukimono, who carried a golden feather. He later became the Wanderer, and before that the Balladeer. A black gas, Tatarigami power from Crystal Marrow used to speed up forging, began sickening workers around the furnace, and Niwa imposed an information blackout.

Quests: Tatara Tales: an eight-quest World Quest series in which the Traveler and Xavier monitor the Mikage Furnace, break the containment dome with the old cannons, fend off Fatui, and finally purify the Tatarigami core. Unlocking it requires finishing Ritou Escape Plan.

Dangers: Electro-aligned wildlife and cicins, Fatui skirmishers, hilichurls, Samachurl, Nobushi, Kairagi and Treasure Hoarders. Before Tatara Tales the area also inflicts Balethunder, a lingering Tatarigami charge that harms anyone who stays.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the furnace is purified and stable since Tatara Tales, and the island is a quiet ruin of industry.

The Tatarasuna Mystery is no longer a mystery to those who followed the Sumeru storyline: Nahida showed the Balladeer the truth. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 is recorded as changing the island.

174.content: About 400 years ago workers at the Mikage Furnace fell ill from black gas of Tatarigami origin while a young kabukimono lived among the Inspector's circle. Public memory has Niwa Hisahide fleeing a crime and the kabukimono purifying the furnace; the truth is that Dottore, posing as a Fontaine mechanic, killed Niwa and used the kabukimono as a test subject. Blame fell on Mikoshi Nagamasa and cost Katsuragi and Nozomu their lives.

175.comment: Tatarasuna: Mikage Furnace and Tatara Tales
175.content: The Mikage Furnace was the engine of Inazuma's Jade Steel, run on Tatarigami energy from Yashiori Island. During the Shogunate's war with the Watatsumi Army, saturation of that energy shut it down and even its auto-restart failed. Xavier raised a containment dome around it and kept the Balethunder in. Shogunate officials worried about halted production; shrine maidens feared the Tatarigami's spill-over, felt even at the Sacred Sakura.

176.content:
Tenryou (also: Tenryou district, Inazuma Commercial Street, Emperor's Land): Tenryou is the commercial heart of Inazuma City, the district below Tenshukaku built around a bustling commercial street. It is one of the city's three parts, with Hanamizaka and Tenshukaku. Adventurers, shoppers, watchmen and Shogunate officials mix here, among teahouses, restaurants, craftsmen, the Adventurers' Guild and a police station.

The word tenryou is not the same as the Tenryou Commission, though they share a root: the Commission is the arm of the Shogunate that keeps public order, and the district is where much of that order is visible, in its watchmen, notices and the nearby Commission headquarters.

Geography: Tenryou lies just below Tenshukaku on the city's hillside, where Inazuma City rises on the southern tip of Narukami Island. Its main feature is a commercial street. Komore Teahouse, Uyuu Restaurant, the Aisa Bathhouse, the police station and a park lie off it.

Places: Commercial street: the Adventurers' Guild receptionist Katheryne, shop owners and street-food vendors.
Komore Teahouse: a members-only teahouse owned by the Yashiro Commission, used by the Kamisato clan as a local base and private meeting place. Its boss is a Shiba Inu named Taroumaru.
Aisa Bathhouse: a Natlan-inspired bathhouse owned and run by the returnee Aikawa Susumu, with rumours of a special investor behind the scenes.
Uyuu Restaurant: run by Okazaki Rikuto and Okazaki Erika.
Police Station: the yoriki Owada and the watchman Uesugi work here.

People: Adventurers such as Furuya Noboru, Satou, Takeda and Yuzu use the street; the researcher Tang Wen, the gourmet Matsumoto and the watchman Sanada are among the regulars. The Guild receptionist Katheryne is here.

Governance: Tenryou is the city district the Tenryou Commission watches most closely. The Commission, led by the Kujou clan, manages security and military affairs and enforced the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees. Its yoriki and doushin are the police of the district.

Culture: Tenryou is the city's shopping and dining quarter. Inazuma City is renowned for family businesses and a low crime rate, and Tenryou's street has lacquerware, textile and netsuke shops, a grocer, a restaurant, a teahouse and street-food vendors.

History: The district's recent history is the war period under the Decrees, then peace after the Archon Quest. Later, after the Natlan events, the Aisa Bathhouse was renovated at the direction of Yumemizuki Mizuki, who became its main investor and decision-maker, adding therapy sessions run by yumekui-baku psychologists.

Travel: The Adventurers' Guild's Inazuma receptionist, Katheryne, works on the commercial street, making it the usual first stop for travellers.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tenryou is a safe, prosperous market district; the Decrees are over.

The Aisa Bathhouse is now a therapy-and-spa venue under Yumemizuki Mizuki. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 plot is set in the district.

177.content: Komore Teahouse is a members-only teahouse in Tenryou, owned by the Yashiro Commission and used by the Kamisato clan as a local base and private meeting place. Only people approved by the Kamisato clan may enter. Its boss is the Shiba Inu Taroumaru, a former ninja dog of the Shuumatsuban, and customers leave their payment in a box after drinking tea.

178.content: The Aisa Bathhouse is an indoor bathhouse in Tenryou inspired by Natlan's hot springs, offering baths, fine dining and, since its renovation, psychotherapy from yumekui-baku. Aikawa Susumu, a returnee from Natlan, is the operator.

179.content:
Tenryou Commission Headquarters (also: Tenryou-bugyou-fu, Tenryou Commission Office): The Tenryou Commission Headquarters is the seat in Inazuma City of the Tenryou Commission, the executive arm of the Shogunate. The Commission is led by the Kujou Clan and handles security and military affairs; in the Archon Quests it is the organisation that carries out the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree. The building has a courtyard exterior and an interior that the story opens in Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage.

The Commission is also the one the story exposes: its head, Kujou Takayuki, concealed the cost of the war from the Shogun and dealt with the Fatui. It remains in disarray, with Kujou Kamaji standing in as acting head.

Geography: The headquarters is a point of interest in Inazuma City on Narukami Island, near Tenshukaku. It has an outdoor courtyard, where Shogunate samurai, yoriki and doushin keep watch, and an interior instance, entered as a quest domain during the Archon Quest. The courtyard NPCs listed on the wiki are Ikeda Soushirou, the yoriki Mikoshi Genjirou and Yata Kouki, and the doushin Watanabe; Okawara Goemon, also a yoriki, is in the interior.

People: The Commission's personnel include Kujou Kamaji (acting clan head), Kujou Sara (General), Kujou Masahito (General), Okawara Goemon (Chief Samurai and Kujou Clan security head), and rank-and-file Shogunate Samurai, yoriki and doushin. Shikanoin Heizou is a Tenryou "Detective". Kujou Takayuki is a past commissioner who is under house arrest.

Governance: Of the three Commissions (Tenryou, Kanjou, Yashiro) in the Tri-Commission, the Tenryou Commission is the Raiden Shogun's executive arm, responsible for security and military matters including enforcement of the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree. The three Commissions share equal authority and can check each other.

History: The Traveler is placed on a wanted list by the Commission after escaping the Vision Hunt Ceremony with Thoma. Later, in Omnipresence Over Mortals, the Traveler and Yae Miko show Kujou Sara a Commission document that omits the cost of the war and a letter to the Fatui. Sara goes to the headquarters to demand an explanation.

Quests: Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage (Chapter II, Act III: Omnipresence Over Mortals). The courtyard is also an ordinary map location with Tenryou NPCs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the headquarters is still the Tenryou Commission's seat. The commissioner's post stays unsettled: Kujou Kamaji acts as head and the Kujou Clan was given more time. Many Tenryou samurai relax at the Aisa Bathhouse.

180.comment: Tenryou Commission Headquarters: Tenryou Commission and the Vision Hunt Decree
180.content: The Commission enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree for the Shogun. Its soldiers fight other people, including the Watatsumi Army, which led to desertions. Distinguish its official line from what individual soldiers privately think.

181.content:
Tenshukaku (also: Tenshu, Shogun's residence): Tenshukaku is the castle keep at the top of Inazuma City on Narukami Island, the residence of the Raiden Shogun and the place from which she rules Inazuma. Built during the Archon War, it is one of the three parts of the city alongside Hanamizaka and Tenryou, and the Tenryou Commission Headquarters stands within its grounds. The Statue of the Omnipresent God, built to hold Visions confiscated under the Vision Hunt Decree, stands before it.

Its name means a castle's tower keep, literally "heavenly protector". Official material describes it as the residence of the most exalted one in Inazuma, standing on the city's highest point and watching over all under the Electro Archon's rule. Entry into the Shogun's presence is tightly controlled.

Geography: Inazuma City rises on cliffs at the southern tip of Narukami Island. Tenshukaku crowns it, above the city's other two parts, Hanamizaka and Tenryou. The Statue of the Omnipresent God stands in front of the keep.

Places: Entrance area, guarded by Shogunate officers; a central courtyard where officials go about their business; a southern tower; the Tenryou Commission Headquarters with its courtyard and offices; and the Shogun's throne chamber, where she receives visitors and where the duel before the throne was fought.

People: The Raiden Shogun resides here: the puppet Shogun who handles Inazuma's affairs, with Ei meditating within her Plane of Euthymia. The Tenryou Commission, led by the Kujou Clan, works out of its headquarters here. Okuzumeshuu guards such as Takeshi control access to the Shogun.

Governance: Tenshukaku is the seat of the Raiden Shogun's rule over the Inazuma Shogunate. The Tenryou Commission, the Shogun's executive arm in charge of security and the military, enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree from here. Inazuman law recognises the duel before the throne, fought in the Shogun's presence with her approval; the loser dies.

History: Inazuma City, Tenshukaku included, was built during the Archon War. A year before the Traveler's arrival the Vision Hunt Decree began, and the statue in front of the keep was built to receive confiscated Visions. In 2.0 the Shogun personally presided over a ceremony there marking the hundredth Vision. In 2.1 the Traveler defeated Signora in a duel before the throne inside Tenshukaku, and the Shogun executed her.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter II: "Amidst Stormy Judgment" (Act II, 2.0) at the statue before the keep; "Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage", "Duel Before the Throne" and "The Omnipresent God" (Act III, 2.1). Raiden Shogun Story Quest: "The Lonesome Euthymia" (Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter, Act I).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tenshukaku remains the Raiden Shogun's residence and seat of rule. The Vision Hunt Decree was abolished in 2.1, Signora died here, and Ei has since reconsidered how she rules.

After the war Ei briefly withdrew into seclusion inside Tenshukaku, temporarily disabling many of the puppet's functions rather than modifying its rules while she worked out the form Eternity should take; she then went out among her people in person. No later story found is set at Tenshukaku in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya).

182.content: A duel before the throne is a contest under Inazuman law, fought in the Raiden Shogun's presence at Tenshukaku with her consent; the loser forfeits their life. Signora called it making the law of the land work for you. The Traveler invoked it against Signora in 2.1; after her defeat the Shogun herself carried out the sentence with the Musou no Hitotachi and, acknowledging the victor's honour, let the Traveler leave Tenshukaku alive.

key: The Altar at The Serpent's Heart
183.comment: The Altar at The Serpent's Heart
183.content:
The Altar at The Serpent's Heart (also: Altar at the Serpent's Heart, Serpent's Heart altar): The altar at the Serpent's Heart is a circular chamber in Enkanomiya with five blue wall panels, each tied to a different Key Sigil. In Evernight, entering a sigil pattern in the right order makes it spawn a chest, an enemy or a spirit, and two world quests start here.

It is where the Traveler first recovers a fragment of the Reins of Revival, and where the afterimage of the resistance leader Supada no Hiko is found, unable to leave.

Geography: The room sits at the heart of the Serpent's Heart island. A mechanism to the north-east switches the area to Evernight, which is needed to use the altar.

Quests: The Heart of Ouroboros (part of From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku) has the Traveler solve the altar's first riddle to receive the first Reins of Revival fragment. In Lotus Eater, an afterimage here, bound by the altar's prison, asks for help recovering his name.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the altar stays as released in 2.4 and has no further role in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content.

184.content:
The Arsenal (also: Tatarasuna Arsenal): The Arsenal is a cave under Tatarasuna in Kannazuka, south of the Mikage Furnace, where the Tatarasuna workers hid a ruined blade. The Daitatara Nagamasa was forged by Inspector Mikoshi Nagamasa and became "Katsuragikiri Nagamasa" after he cut down his yoriki Katsuragi with it.

Inside lies a Luxurious Chest holding the diagram for forging a replica of that sword.

Geography: The cave lies south of the Mikage Furnace; the gate is near the water on its eastern side. The surrounding furnace area is blocked by a Containment Field until part of the Tatara Tales quest is completed.

History: Per the wiki account, Mikoshi Nagamasa, Tatarasuna's Shogunate inspector, grew fond of bladesmithing and forged the Daitatara Nagamasa with the Vice Armory Officer Miyazaki. His group celebrated: Nozomu painted the blade, while Katsuragi and a nameless wandering eccentric performed a sword dance. Soon afterward the group broke up.

Quests: Tatara Tales opens the furnace area; the Rather Aged Notes scattered around the Mikage Furnace recount the incident, and they read as if seized in a raid on the Fatui.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Arsenal stands unchanged as an explorable cave, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes the Tatarasuna story.

185.content:
The Emanant Skylight (also: Emanant Skylights): The Emanant Skylight names three places in Enkanomiya where a pool of ghostfish waits during Evernight. Gliding into the fish lifts the Traveler to a time tunnel that opens onto one of the three Locus subareas.

The fish only appear after the world quest The Three Great Martial Trials has been started, and Bathysmal Vishaps guard each pool.

Places: The skylight at The Narrows leads to Yachimatahiko's Locus; the one at the Evernight Temple to Yachimatahime's Locus; the one at the Serpent's Heart to Kunado's Locus.

Quests: The Three Great Martial Trials starts with Eboshi (Erebos), who calls herself an auxiliary of Sangonomiya, one of Enkanomiya's shrine maidens. She says the older trial to win the branch was meant to keep the full truth from later generations, whereas she wanted records kept, so Watatsumi Omikami let her add a path leading to the secrets. Starting the quest reveals the three Locus subareas.

Atmosphere: Dim ceiling openings pouring light into dark cavern waters, with fish that rise like a stairway of ghosts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the three skylights remain tied to The Three Great Martial Trials, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes them.

186.content:
The Narrows (also: Narrows of Enkanomiya): The Narrows is a ruined subarea of Enkanomiya. In the earliest times it was squeezed between the mountain face and an area called the Roundlands, which gave it its name. Strange tectonic shifts in Byakuyakoku later dropped the Roundlands into the depths, so the Narrows widened considerably. Its ruins hide a chamber that only appears when the land shifts between Whitenight and Evernight.

That chamber, sealed by a Sunfire Phantasm, held one of the Reins of Revival fragments the Traveler sought in The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent. A hiding place used by Byakuyakoku's resistance also lies here.

Geography: A broad ruin-filled stretch of the Enkanomiya underground, with cliffs on one side and, where the Roundlands once stood, open depths on the other. The land shifts between Whitenight and Evernight, revealing or hiding structures.

Places: The Narrows ruins, and the hidden chamber for the fragment; a hiding place opened by a lantern puzzle during Whitenight, where an afterimage waits.

People: No living inhabitants. The guide Aru speaks of the Narrows, and an afterimage in the hiding place is met during Lotus Eater.

History: From the Byakuyakoku texts: in the earliest times the Narrows lay between the mountain face and the Roundlands. Tectonic upheaval brought the Roundlands down into the depths and widened the place.

Quests: The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent (the fragment) and Lotus Eater (the hiding place).

Dangers: The wiki lists no special hazards for this subarea beyond Enkanomiya's usual enemies.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Narrows are unchanged and the chamber is empty.

No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content touches Enkanomiya.

187.content:
The Serpent's Bowels (also: Serpent's Bowels): The Serpent's Bowels is a quiet subarea of Enkanomiya, the underground realm of Byakuyakoku. The wiki lists the Sangonomiya Shrine as its entrance. It is a damp network of caverns with silently flowing underground rivers, and no battle music plays here. It holds the giant Dragonbone Flower.

Its waters are home to fish, and the area includes a waterfall near which a rusted blade of the Iwakura Clan can be found, a link to Narukami Island's Byakko Plain. A note found here recalls how Watatsumi's people unwittingly fed the Bathysmal Vishaps.

Geography: Caverns and tunnels of wet stone, a great gate and rivers that run in silence. The fishing point's in-game description suggests, as speculation, that these waters might link the place to the outside world.

Places: The Dragonbone Flower: a giant flower atop which, in Lotus Eater, the Traveler pours the Waters of Lethe. A great gate, a fishing point and a spot with damp Scribbled Notes.

People: No residents. Only scribbled notes remain, left by an unnamed traveller who journeyed with Watatsumi's chosen hero.

History: The Scribbled Notes say the Bathysmal Vishaps suddenly became active, but a clerk of the Sangonomiya Shrine convinced the writer and the hero to spare them. The people of Watatsumi, throwing food offerings into the Moon-Bathed Deep, had been feeding the creatures, and the clerk said they could no longer threaten humanity, so Enkanomiya was best returned to them.

Quests: Lotus Eater, in which the flower is watered; the Hidden Exploration Objectives Iwakura Art's Downfall and Adonis' Abandoned Safehouse touch the region.

Dangers: No battle music; the wiki does not list any enemies here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is unchanged: empty, quiet, with the flower still standing.

No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content touches Enkanomiya.

188.content: A giant flower in the Serpent's Bowels. In Lotus Eater, the Traveler pours the Waters of Lethe on it, waits until the next daily reset and takes the Dragonbone Orb; the orb is said to make one forget. The Waters of Lethe flow near the Evernight Temple and do not themselves cause forgetfulness when drunk.

189.content:
The Serpent's Heart (also: Serpent's Heart, Delphi, Heart of Ouroboros): The Serpent's Heart is a subarea of Enkanomiya, the underground realm of Byakuyakoku. It was made with the power of Sunfire Phantasms, to guard secrets, imprison criminals and worship the great imaginary serpent Ouroboros. At its centre stands an altar regarded as the heart of that Cosmic Serpent, a sealing device for storing important objects. Its oldest name was Delphi, the Serpent's Land.

Its name predates the arrival of Orobashi, the Watatsumi Omikami, and did not change after it. The Traveler retrieved a Reins of Revival fragment from the altar during the quest The Heart of Ouroboros.

Geography: A cavernous zone of Enkanomiya's underground sea. It is where space itself is said to overlap, a phenomenon the early Enkanomiyans noticed when they first found the place, and which they used to build the prison-vault.

Places: The Altar at the Serpent's Heart: the vault itself; patterns entered here retrieve stored objects. The Emanant Skylight: a spot with a pool and a Time Tunnel that leads to Kunado's Locus once the trials begin.

People: No standing population. An afterimage at the altar names itself Supada no Hiko (Spartacus), a resistance leader imprisoned here; he has forgotten his own name until the Traveler restores it. The guide Aru supplied information about the fragments during The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent.

History: The Byakuyakoku Collection describes the site as discovered with its overlapping-space phenomenon already present. Ancestors later built the Serpent's Heart on it. Before Orobashi arrived it was known as the Heart of Ouroboros; Delphi kept its name afterwards.

Quests: The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent (the fragment hunt), The Heart of Ouroboros (a Reins of Revival fragment is taken from the altar), and Lotus Eater (a side quest begun at the altar).
