Dangers: Ruin Sentinels guard parts of the zone, and Abyss and hilichurl enemies are found in Enkanomiya generally. Switching between Whitenight and Evernight is part of exploring safely.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the altar's prize is gone and the prison is empty save for afterimages.

The Byakuyakoku texts record the sealing of the depths and the emigration of Watatsumi's people; the Serpent's Heart is a relic of that age. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content revisits it.

190.comment: The Serpent's Heart: Delphi and Ouroboros
190.content: The Enkanomiyans revered snakes even before Orobashi became their patron. Ouroboros, also called the great imaginary serpent or Cosmic Serpent, was worshipped from the earliest times, and Delphi meant the land of snakes. After Orobashi came, they worshipped both. Ancient art depicts Ouroboros as scaleless and Orobashi as coral-adorned.

191.comment: The Serpent's Heart: Supada no Hiko
191.content: In the Lotus Eater quest an afterimage in the altar says he led a resistance against Byakuyakoku's nobles and that his students, whom he calls his children, hold the nation's hope. He forgot his name under the prison's erosion; the Traveler restores it from an ancient tablet naming him as Supada no Hiko and the 'Righteous', condemned as a bandit.

192.content:
Tokoyo Reisen (also: River Lethe, Waters of Lethe): Tokoyo Reisen, once known as the River Lethe, is a stream in the Evernight Temple area of Enkanomiya. Its water glows faintly in the dark. In the World Quest Lotus Eater the Traveler collects the Waters of Lethe here to grow a Dragonbone Orb, a fruit whose scent calms the mind and makes people forget their worries.

The water itself does not erase memory; only the orb made with its help does. The wiki notes the name echoes the River Lethe of Greek myth, whose water made the dead forget.

Geography: The stream runs near the Evernight Temple in Enkanomiya and is one of the places the Traveler is sent to in Lotus Eater. The water shines weakly in the darkness and looks unremarkable to Paimon on first sight.

History: Lotus Eater tells how a resistance member in Byakuyakoku, Adonis, and his comrades sold Dragonbone Orbs to fund their cause against the nobles. Soon they found that members of the resistance began to avoid conflict and asked to leave, which Adonis blames on contentment: when oppressed peoples grow satisfied they cease to resist. He suspects the orb's formula may have been leaked by the rulers, though he cannot say. He tells the Traveler that the orbs can only be made with the water of Tokoyo Reisen.

Quests: Lotus Eater starts at the Altar at the Serpent's Heart and requires The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent. Its steps include going to Tokoyo Reisen, obtaining the Waters of Lethe, going to the top of the Dragonbone Flower, watering it, and collecting the Dragonbone Orb after a day. Afterwards the orb can be sold in a side objective.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tokoyo Reisen is unchanged and still the source of the Waters of Lethe. No later story involves it.

193.content: A Dragonbone Orb is a rare fruit a Dragonbone Flower bears when watered with the Waters of Lethe. Its fragrance relaxes the mind and sweeps away worry, so it fetched a high price, and eventually the resistance in Byakuyakoku used its sale for funds. Its effect on the buyer is forgetting. The item text for the Waters of Lethe says the water by itself will not cause forgetting.

194.content:
Tsurumi Island: Tsurumi Island is a remote island of Inazuma that was long wrapped in a dense fog and avoided for years. It holds the remains of two vanished peoples. The older one was linked to Celestia and lies buried underground. The later one was a tribe that worshipped the Thunderbird, Kanna Kapatcir. When the boy Ruu was sacrificed to her, the Thunderbird destroyed the tribe in grief and rage and cursed the island to relive its final days. The Traveler helped Ruu's spirit keep his promise to sing for her again. That lifted the curse and the fog, and the island's spirits are now passing on.

No one lives there now apart from hilichurls, riftwolves and old automatons. Kama, who ferried the Traveler over from Ritou and has since been seen travelling with Sumida, is the tribe's only known living descendant.

Geography: A hilly island of grassland, beaches and ruins. Mt. Kanna, the tribe's sacred ground where the Thunderbird dwelt, rises in the centre. The Moshiri Ceremonial Site was where the rites were held. Shirikoro Peak and Chirai Shrine stand over a network of underground ruins. The coasts include Oina Beach and Wakukau Shoal, and the open Autake Plains lie inland. Wooden "Perches" for offerings once stood around the island.

People: The island has no living inhabitants. Until the curse was lifted, illusions of the tribe re-enacted the final ceremony. Ruu alone among them became self-aware: he noticed changes on the island and the passing of time without understanding why. After the curse ended, spirits of the dead appeared, and a mysterious "Boatman" began ferrying them to a "golden land" once their last wishes were settled.

Culture: The Thunderbird tribe worshipped Kapatcir with fear and gratitude, read her unpredictable actions as divine revelations, and chose shamans to offer blood sacrifices. They called to each other through the fog with the Maushiro, at first an instrument made from her feathers and later a wooden imitation. They were taught never to leave the island, since anyone who did was believed lost in the "sea of darkness". The fog, they thought, was the Thunderbird's protection.

History: In the age of the ancient unified civilisation, a people connected to Celestia lived on Tsurumi and worshipped the Three Moons. "Strange objects" later fell from the heavens, destroying that civilisation and producing the fog. Kanna Kapatcir, the Thunderbird who made the island her home, saw this and left the fog in place although she could have dispersed it. Later a new tribe came to worship her. She paid them no heed until, more than 1,500 years ago, the boy Ruu's song pierced the clouds. She landed beside him, he gave her the name "Kanna Kapatcir" (Great Eagle of the Storm), and he promised to sing for her again. When she returned she found him dead, sacrificed by his own people, his blood in a ritual cup. To her this was the murder of an innocent and a broken promise. She razed the tribe with lightning and cursed the island to repeat its last days until she heard his song again. She then flew to Seirai Island, where Ei later killed her.

Atmosphere: Before the curse lifted: silence, grey fog that turned travellers around, and illusory villagers who acted strangely and vanished between visits. During the final confrontation the fog turned red and crimson lightning struck. Afterwards: open grass, waves, wind over ruined platforms, and the occasional spirit asking a stranger for one last favour.

Dangers: The fog once teleported intruders back to the island's edge. Riftwolves, Thundercraven rifthounds, hilichurls, Abyss Mages and Ruin automatons roam today. A Thunder Manifestation formed from the Thunderbird's rage appeared in the hollow of Mt. Kanna.

Travel: Tsurumi lies apart from the main islands and was reached by boat with Kama's help. Before the questline, only the southern peninsula and the eastern isles near the Statue of The Seven could be reached.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the curse and the fog are gone, and the island's spirits are moving on with the Boatman. Tsurumi remains uninhabited. No Tsurumi-specific content appears in 6.x-7.1.

195.comment: Tsurumi Island: Ruu and the Thunderbird
195.content: Ruu was a boy of Tsurumi's Thunderbird tribe whose song drew down the Thunderbird. He named her Kanna Kapatcir and promised to sing for her again. Believing his sacrifice would set things right for his people, he let himself be sacrificed. She saw it as murder and a broken promise, destroyed the tribe, and bound the island in a looping curse until she could hear his song again. Through the loop Ruu lived on as an aware illusion. In 2.2 the Traveler, with Kama, helped him understand what she had wanted and brought him to Seirai to sing, ending the curse.

196.content:
Tsurumi Underground Ruins: The Tsurumi Underground Ruins are a network of caverns beneath Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. They link Shirikoro Peak, whose entrance is at the mountain's base under a Perch, with Chirai Shrine, whose entrance is beneath its ruins. They hold remains of the Thunderbird Civilization and of an even earlier civilization, together with murals.

The murals and torch puzzles are the main clues to a human civilization that predates the Thunderbird's worshippers. Ruin machines guard the halls.

Geography: Long underground passages between the two entrances, with a mural room, a submerged room and several Ruins Torches. Mysterious Carvings can be used to reveal hidden murals.

Places: The Mural Room holds three mountain murals: Shirikoro Peak on the left, the mountain on the road to the Moshiri Ceremonial Site in the middle, and Mt. Kanna on the right. Other murals near the Ruins Torches indicate puzzle solutions, and carvings reveal one beside the submerged room.

History: Long ago a unified human civilization existed across Teyvat, including Tsurumi Island, and left murals through the underground ruins. Above it, over 1,500 years ago, the Thunderbird Civilization settled the island and worshipped Kanna Kapatcir; its people were later destroyed after the sacrifice of Ruu.

Dangers: Elite Ruin Cruisers, Ruin Destroyers, Ruin Sentinels and Ruin Scouts. Some areas are flooded; Electro current puzzles and torch puzzles block doors.

Travel: Enter at Shirikoro Peak (base of the mountain beneath the Perch) or from beneath Chirai Shrine's ruins. The A Particularly Particular Author steps show how to open the Shirikoro entrance.

Quests: Gameplay note: three Ruins Torch puzzles require the Peculiar Pinion gadget from Octave of the Maushiro (2.2). Solving them is a prerequisite for the achievement "Guessing Game". The hidden objective "Tsurumi's Mountain Murals" begins here and needs the Pinion and the three Star-Shaped Gems.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins are abandoned. The Thunderbird's curse was lifted in 2.2, and no later content adds to the site.

197.comment: Tsurumi Underground Ruins: Tsurumi Mountain Murals
197.content: In the hidden exploration objective, the Traveler places the three Star-Shaped Gems in the mountain murals of the underground ruins. Electro Seelie fly out and mark the locations, at Mt. Kanna, Shirikoro Peak and the mountain on the way to the Moshiri Ceremonial Site, each guiding the player to a spot. Completing it gives an Exquisite Chest and then a Luxurious Chest, and is a prerequisite for the achievement "Guessing Game".

198.content:
Uyuu Restaurant (also: Uyuu-tei, Uyuu Pagoda): Uyuu Restaurant is a tavern-style restaurant on the commercial street of Tenryou in Inazuma City, owned by Okazaki Rikuto, who calls it an izakaya, with Okazaki Erika cooking and serving. A bulletin board beside the entrance carries messages from regular customers, including General Gorou. Its Japanese name Uyuu-tei is written with characters that echo a Chinese word for "nothing" or "nonexistence".

The owner is a retired figure of the Tenryou Commission who still gets visits from yoriki and doushin. Patrons use the bulletin board to thank him, tease him, ask him for favours and leave letters and gifts in his keeping, and he answers them there.

Places: Uyuu Restaurant has a ground floor with tables and an upstairs with a mural. A bulletin board stands by the entrance, and an aged temari, a children's ball with scars and burrs, sits by a table; the name Okazaki Seishimaru is written on it. Outside, the food critic Matsumoto can usually be found.

People: Rikuto is the owner, an older man who was once with the Tenryou Commission and says he had a stand-up reputation there; yoriki and doushin still ask his advice. He praises Erika's cooking as among the best in Inazuma City, drinks sake at the restaurant and tells a young Traveler there is no hurry about drinking. Erika is the cook. When asked how they met, she says it is a long story: when she was young she was ordered to watch an important figure at the Tenryou Commission, and she thanks the archons he eventually retired so they could marry.

Governance: It is a private business owned by a retired Tenryou Commission man. Customers include officials, soldiers and travellers, judging by the messages left there.

Culture: The bulletin board is the restaurant's best-known institution, a place where people leave messages and the owner answers them. The messages are sometimes comic and sometimes moving.

History: The restaurant is first mentioned in Someone's Drifting Bottle, a message found in the world from version 1.2. The bottle's note, written by Hiromi to Yan'er, asks whether she remembers Uyuu Restaurant, says they will meet there and encloses money for wine. In the 2.0 world quest "Hiromi's Watch" the Traveler delivers the bottle's contents to Yan'er, who says the restaurant seems a fine place and that she will go there for drinks, and the Traveler later reminds Hiromi of the name.

Atmosphere: A drinking house with sake on the table, a bulletin board crowded with notes and a landlord who greets customers as youngsters. The board's messages show soldiers, adventurers and officials passing through under the shadow of the Sakoku Decree.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the restaurant is open under Rikuto and Erika; the board has Sakoku-era messages plus ones added after Radiant Sakura.

199.content: Rikuto is the owner of Uyuu Restaurant, a retired Tenryou Commission man who drinks sake at his own table. He answers the board's messages in person-to-person replies, calls young customers youngsters, offers barbecued skewers, and says Seishimaru was once a relative. His exact former rank is not stated.

200.content: Erika is the cook and waitress at Uyuu Restaurant, who welcomes customers and takes orders. She was once assigned to keep watch on an important Tenryou Commission figure, who later retired, and is implied to be Rikuto's wife.

201.comment: Uyuu Restaurant: Someone's Drifting Bottle and Hiromi
201.content: A drifting bottle found in waters southeast of Dragonspine holds a letter to a lost friend suggesting a reunion at Uyuu Restaurant with money for wine. The Traveler carries it to Hiromi, then to Yan'er, who says she does not know any officer who catches thieves but may go for drinks. Shun, the third friend, says the three drank at Uyuu the day before the Sakoku Decree took effect.

key: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon
202.comment: Uyuu Restaurant: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon Cameo
202.content: In the limited-time 7.1 event "Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon" (24 September to 12 October 2026), Rikuto, Erika and Matsumoto appear in the event's cast. Rikuto says it feels like being young again, and Erika wonders how long it has been since they took a trip together, suggesting they cook another hundred dishes together. Matsumoto notes that the food is seasoned boldly and says he will talk to Anna when he gets back. The event is canon but time-limited.

203.content:
Violet Court: Violet Court is a Domain of Mastery in Kannazuka, Inazuma, an altar where violet sakura bloom eternal. Its description recounts that in the ancient past the mountains rose higher than the sky and the earth was larger than the dome of heaven, until the mirror shattered and the oceans arose; in these legends the court of the primeval sakura was severed from the other islands. Monsters now storm the altar.

Clearing it yields Talent level-up materials (the Transience, Elegance and Light series by weekday). It was added in Version 2.0. The enemies are Electro-themed: Hilichurls, Nobushi, Treasure Hoarders and, at the top level, the Kairagi pair.

Geography: An island of Kannazuka with a sakura-ringed altar. The domain entrance island appears on the map once the Statue of The Seven on Narukami Island is unlocked, even though the domain belongs to Kannazuka.

Dangers: Hilichurls and Electro Hilichurl Grenadiers and Shooters, Crackling Axe Mitachurls, Nobushi (Jintouban, Hitsukeban, Kikouban), Treasure Hoarders, and at level IV the Kairagi: Fiery Might and Kairagi: Dancing Thunder.

History: Only legend: the sakura court was cut off when the mirror shattered (the wiki links the wording to the war of the funerary flame, but the domain itself gives no names). The Sacred Sakura on Mt. Yougou is the better-known primeval sakura in Inazuma.

204.content:
Vishap Research Lab (also: Bathysmal Vishap research site, Byakuyakoku research lab): The Vishap Research Lab is a hidden laboratory of ancient Byakuyakoku in Enkanomiya, where researchers studied and bred Bathysmal Vishaps (the "Dragonheirs of the Depths") under the personal direction of Watatsumi Omikami. It does not appear on the map. The Traveler can reach it through a phase gate on the small island north of the Dainichi Mikoshi and finds there the afterimage of a researcher called Michiya, who guards the experiment records.

The lab is the starting point of the world quest "Tricolor File", which yields the Bathysmal Vishap Experimental Records, one of the five lost books in "Collection of Dragons and Snakes". Its text shows a programme of controlled breeding, intelligence tests and blood-grafting that was meant to protect Enkanomiya from a prophecy, and whose staff disagreed about whether to keep or burn the results.

Geography: The lab lies outside the ordinary Enkanomiya map. To reach it, go to the small island north of the Dainichi Mikoshi, either by gliding down from the northmost waypoint of the Dainichi Mikoshi or by gliding from the ghostfish cluster at the far east of The Narrows, and then use the Phase Gate at the island's northmost point.

People: The only resident is Michiya, the afterimage of a researcher of the lab, one of the Shades of Tokoyo. The quest that begins with him can only be started during Evernight. Like most shades he is a translucent figure without distinguishing features and does not seem to realise he is only an afterimage; Paimon notes it in an aside.

Governance: The programme was directed by Watatsumi Omikami in person. The records say the research team was split between those who wanted to burn the records and those who wanted to save them for a later generation that might forgive them. Michiya favoured burning but accepted the hidden-records compromise.

History: The records describe a programme on the Dragonheirs of the Depths. Researchers raised vishaps in altered environments and found they could awaken or generate traits for their descendants: a heat-resistant vishap raised in cold gave offspring with more body fat, more sleep and the Cryo element, while descendants returned to heat chose heat resistance again without gaining Pyro. After four generations the vishaps' language ability approached that of a twelve-year-old student, and the writer argued the experiments should stop, citing the prophecy that the Dragon Sovereign of Water would be born in human form, which they did not want to happen in Enkanomiya.

Dangers: The locked cell holds a Rimebiter Bathysmal Vishap Hatchling that is released when the elemental monument is lit. Bathysmal Vishaps hate man-made light and can drain a fighter's energy or, if energy runs out, health. Paimon warns that lighting the monument will summon dangerous vishaps, so prepare first.

Quests: "Tricolor File" (World Quest, 2.4; requires "The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent"): speak to Michiya, then light the Cryo monument to open the cell and obtain the Bathysmal Vishap Experimental Records. The records can be obtained without the quest. "Collection of Dragons and Snakes" requires them: Ema, an afterimage in The Narrows library, wants five lost books returned, and handing in the records contributes the fourth volume of The Byakuyakoku Collection.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the lab is unchanged: a hidden, abandoned Enkanomiya site whose records are in the Traveler's archive. No content from 5.x to 7.1 mentions it. Enkanomiya itself is little known outside Inazuma.

205.comment: Vishap Research Lab: The Bathysmal Vishap Experimental Records
205.content: Volume 4 of The Byakuyakoku Collection. It is signed with no individual name and kept in the file numbering that mixes Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, Ether and Void categories. It contains the evolution experiments, the intelligence study, and the grafting trials directed by Watatsumi Omikami. The final entry praises Omikami as "gracious and beneficent" and notes that none of the Dragonheirs died in the experiments. Volume 5 in the same collection, a puzzle book for children, echoes the same prophecy and warns against making vishaps sound adorable lest children lower their guard.

206.content: Michiya is a Shade of Tokoyo, the afterimage of a researcher of the Vishap Research Lab. He speaks as one who feels guilt and duty: he will keep watch until departure, believes the research team did wrong, and will not give the records away easily. After "Tricolor File" he refuses to say more. He expects that he and his colleagues are about to start a new life above the surface.

207.content:
Wakukau Shoal (also: Wakukau-hama): Wakukau Shoal is a shoreline subarea of Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. It has little lore of its own, but in the world quest The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna it is the first place where the Traveler uses the Thunderbird feather on a Mysterious Carving and is drawn into a memory of Kanna Kapatcir.

It is part of the search for the boy Ruu, who is not found here.

Geography: A rocky shoreline with a rock arch, a large camp site and cliffs above. Mysterious Carvings and a Thunder Sakura Bough stand here, and Sea Ganoderma grows along the shore.

History: Using the feather here summons two waves of monsters, ending with a Thunderhelm Lawachurl. A voice asks where someone is, and the feather that drops shows the Traveler a vision from the Thunderbird's view of Tsurumi Island under fog. She hears the voices of boars, humans, squirrels, lizards and Wen Kamuy, and then a clear song in the rain, unlike the war songs of the boars and the choruses of the fish.

Quests: The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna (2.2): the first of three feather sites, followed by Oina Beach and the Autake Plains.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Electro Samachurls, Hydro slimes, Ruin Guards and Thundercraven Rifthounds, depending on the day.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no later canon read for this entry changes the shoal.

208.content:
Watatsumi Island: Watatsumi Island is the Inazuman island farthest from the capital, a lush land of giant coral and brightly coloured plants unlike anything elsewhere. The serpent god Orobashi raised it from his own coral some two thousand years ago so that his people could leave the undersea realm of Enkanomiya. Ei later killed him, but the islanders still worship him as the Watatsumi Omikami. Their Divine Priestess, Sangonomiya Kokomi, governs from Sangonomiya Shrine. Watatsumi led the armed resistance against the Vision Hunt Decree, and since the decree's repeal it has kept an uneasy ceasefire with the Shogunate.

Its distance from the capital let the islanders build their own culture and customs, and its strained relationship with the Shogun is common knowledge across Inazuma.

Geography: Mountains, waterfalls and towering coral surround Sangonomiya Shrine at the island's centre. Bourou Village stands nearby. In the south lies Suigetsu Pool, with ancient ruins above and below the water, and Mouun Shrine overlooks the sea from a high cliff. A pool beneath Sangonomiya Shrine, the Moon-Bathed Deep, is the way down to Enkanomiya.

Places: - **Sangonomiya Shrine**: seat of the Sangonomiya Clan and headquarters of the resistance; the present shrine was built after Orobashi's death.
- **Bourou Village**: an ancient village whose people trace their ancestry to the deep; the Watatsumi Army's training camp and rallying point.
- **Suigetsu Pool**: a pool hiding the sunken mansion of Umigozen, a once-famous Inazuman figure (the domain Palace in a Pool).
- **Mouun Shrine**: a cliff-top shrine overlooking the ocean.

People: The islanders descend from the people of Enkanomiya. Kokomi is Divine Priestess and the resistance's strategist; Gorou is her general. Shrine maidens trained at Sangonomiya Shrine serve Orobashi rather than the Sacred Sakura; they include Izumi Naki, Mochizuki, Tsuyuko, Shizuru and Miwa.

History: Orobashi, a god who fled the Archon War, became the god of the people of Enkanomiya and replaced their ancient language with Narukami's. About two thousand years ago he broke off coral from his body to create Watatsumi Island, his people climbed up to it, and he taught them to farm and smelt. For years they respected their border with the Shogunate. Driven by famine, they then urged him to invade fertile Yashiori Island, and Ei killed him there. Watatsumi accepted her rule, but tension lasted. Under the Vision Hunt Decree it broke into open war, with the Watatsumi Army fighting the Tenryou Commission's forces at Yashiori and Kannazuka.

Culture: The island's customs grew apart from Narukami's, rooted in descent from the deep and in reverence for the sea serpent. The Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri ritual protects the soil and needs a Bloodbranch (Jade) Coral Branch from Enkanomiya.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 a ceasefire holds and the island keeps its own army as a peacekeeping force, rebuilding its economy and clearing out the Fatui. Talks on Watatsumi's return to Shogunate rule have made some progress but are paused. No Watatsumi-specific story content appears in 6.x-7.1.

209.comment: Watatsumi Island: Orobashi and the Watatsumi Omikami
209.content: Orobashi no Mikoto, the giant serpent god worshipped on Watatsumi as the Watatsumi Omikami, led his people up from Enkanomiya and raised Watatsumi Island from his coral. When famine struck he invaded Yashiori Island and was slain there by Ei's Musou no Hitotachi. His lingering power became the Tatarigami, and his remains still lie on Yashiori. He had been condemned by the Heavenly Principles for reading forbidden knowledge, and he chose the invasion partly to meet that fate. His people still revere him.

210.content:
Yachimatahiko's Locus (also: Yachimatahiko no Chi, Yachimatahiko's Land): Yachimatahiko's Locus is a hidden subarea of Enkanomiya in Inazuma, introduced in Version 2.4. It was the site of one of the three Towers of the Three Realms, built to keep harmony between the human, elemental (vishap) and abyssal realms. It appears on the map only after the world quest Erebos' Secret begins.

It is one of three trial grounds opened by the shade Eboshi, an auxiliary of Sangonomiya and a shrine maiden of Enkanomiya. Here the Jibashiri Uda, in charge of the trial of "wisdom", sets the Traveler a puzzle of four Flames of the High Gate.

Geography: The Locus is reached by a Time Tunnel at The Emanant Skylight in The Narrows once Eboshi has raised it, or can be glided to from above the Dainichi Mikoshi. Most of it is shrouded by a barrier until the trial progresses. It holds a Teleport Waypoint, a Day-Night Mechanism and Triangular Mechanisms.

Quests: Yachimatahiko's Trial is part of The Three Great Martial Trials and Erebos' Secret. The Traveler passes through the Time Tunnel, speaks to an afterimage before the seal, then releases four Flames of the High Gate using the Day-Night Mechanism (Whitenight or Evernight) and the Triangular Mechanisms. Uda then acknowledges the Traveler's valour, calling it "extensive and meticulous". Uda says that was a praise the Divine Priestess once gave skilled youths, later written on pennants at Jibashiri headquarters.

History: Per The Byakuyakoku Collection (via the wiki), the people of Enkanomiya built the Towers of the Three Realms at the borders of Byakuyakoku to stabilise it, as it sat on the edge of the human, elemental and abyssal realms. The towers are hidden through secret arts and can be summoned only by shrine maidens like Eboshi and the Vassals of Watatsumi. Their ancient names are forgotten.

Dangers: Anemo, Hydro and Geo Specters appear in the area.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, unchanged: the trial is complete and the tower stays hidden unless raised by Eboshi.

211.content:
Yachimatahime's Locus (also: Yachimatahime no Chi, Yachimatahime's Land): Yachimatahime's Locus is a hidden subarea of Enkanomiya in Inazuma, introduced in Version 2.4. It was the site of one of the three Towers of the Three Realms, built to keep harmony between the human, elemental (vishap) and abyssal realms. It appears on the map only after the world quest Erebos' Secret begins.

It is one of three trial grounds opened by the shade Eboshi, an auxiliary of Sangonomiya and a shrine maiden of Enkanomiya. Here the Jibashiri Eki, in charge of the trial of "insight", sets the Traveler a puzzle of four Flames of the High Gate.

Geography: The Locus is reached by a Time Tunnel at The Emanant Skylight in Evernight Temple once Eboshi has raised it, or can be glided to from above the Dainichi Mikoshi. Most of it is shrouded by a barrier until the trial progresses. It holds a Teleport Waypoint and Phase Gates.

Quests: Yachimatahime's Trial is part of The Three Great Martial Trials and Erebos' Secret. The Traveler passes through the Time Tunnel, speaks to the afterimage before the seal, and releases four Flames of the High Gate. Eki then acknowledges the Traveler's valour, saying it shows enough insight to seek an eel in winter, a reference to the very small unagi fry of the breeding season.

History: Per The Byakuyakoku Collection (via the wiki), the people of Enkanomiya built the Towers of the Three Realms at the borders of Byakuyakoku to stabilise it, as it sat on the edge of the human, elemental and abyssal realms. The towers are hidden through secret arts and can be summoned only by shrine maidens like Eboshi and the Vassals of Watatsumi. Their ancient names are forgotten.

Dangers: Anemo and Hydro Specters appear in the area.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, unchanged: the trial is complete and the tower stays hidden unless raised by Eboshi.

212.content:
Yashiori Island (also: Yashiori-jima): Yashiori Island is a rain-lashed island in Inazuma, near Watatsumi Island. Here the serpent god Orobashi, worshipped by the people of Watatsumi, was slain by the Electro Archon's legendary Musou no Hitotachi, which split the island in two and left a canyon, Musoujin Gorge. The god's bones lie scattered across the island, and its lingering will, the Tatarigami curse, brings storms, sickness and madness. The Shogunate and the Watatsumi Army fought over it during the Vision Hunt Decree war.

The island yields Crystal Marrow, a mineral drawn from Orobashi's remains, which has long made it worth contesting. Its ancient wards, the Narukami Pillars, kept the curse in check until they were destroyed shortly before the Traveler's arrival.

Geography: A rugged, wet island whose east is cut by the narrow, deep Musoujin Gorge. Orobashi's colossal skull and bones form landmarks (the Serpent's Head). Subareas include Fort Fujitou, a Watatsumi Army camp; Fort Mumei, the ruins of an ancient city; Higi Village; Jakotsu Mine; Nazuchi Beach; the Serpent's Head; and the gorge. Local specialties include Crystal Marrow, Naku Weed, Onikabuto, Dendrobium and Sea Ganoderma.

History: Towards the end of the Archon War, about 2,000 years ago, Orobashi, the Watatsumi Omikami, invaded Yashiori Island, perhaps because Watatsumi was starving and pressed by Celestia's decree. Ei, then acting for her sister Makoto, waged a brutal war and killed Orobashi with the Musou no Hitotachi, splitting the island and leaving its remains. Its lingering will became the Tatarigami, which the Shogunate suppressed with Narukami Pillars. Recently, radicals in the Watatsumi Army, urged on by a Fatui mole, destroyed the wards and unleashed the curse.

Dangers: Tatarigami-tainted enemies (shown with a black aura), Kairagi, Nobushi, hilichurls, Treasure Hoarders and Ruin Machines; a Maguu Kenki guards the final ward. Constant thunder, Balethunder in the gorge, and illness for anyone without a Vision or similar sensitivity.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the island is quiet but scarred. The civil war fought over it ended when the Vision Hunt Decree was revoked (2.1). The wards were repaired in Orobashi's Legacy, the storms have eased, and the Tatarigami linger.

No Yashiori event is shown in 6.x or 7.0-7.1; the island is described as of the last released content.

213.comment: Yashiori Island: Orobashi's Death and the Musou no Hitotachi
213.content: Orobashi was a coral-bodied serpent god who ruled Enkanomiya and then Watatsumi Island, having learned forbidden history that Celestia wished hidden. It invaded Yashiori Island and was slain by Ei's Musou no Hitotachi, which tore Musoujin Gorge across the island and left the serpent's remains. Watatsumi's people still worship it.

214.content: The Tatarigami is the curse formed of Orobashi's will and power. Wards called Narukami Pillars suppress it; when they fall it brings storms, sickness and madness. Vision-bearers resist it best, and Crystal Marrow from the remains is mined.

215.content: Higi Village was devastated by the war and then by the Tatarigami. It is nearly empty: Washizu, the chief, has gone mad; Yasumoto is a pharmacist trying to cure the illness; Chouji, a boy, gathers Crystal Marrow near Jakotsu Mine.

216.comment: Yashiori Island: Fort Fujitou and Fort Mumei
216.content: Fort Fujitou is a Watatsumi Army camp where Kaji studies the weather. Fort Mumei is an ancient city's ruins that rose from the sea after the first three wards were repaired; a Maguu Kenki guards its final ward.

217.content:
Yashiro Commission Headquarters (also: Yashiro Commission HQ, Sha-bugyou Headquarters, Yashiro Bugyo headquarters): The Yashiro Commission Headquarters is the working seat of the Yashiro Commission, the branch of Inazuma's Tri-Commission that manages shrines, festivals and cultural events. It occupies the main building of the Kamisato Estate in Inazuma City. The Kamisato Clan leads the Commission: Kamisato Ayato is clan head and Yashiro Commissioner, and his younger sister Kamisato Ayaka, the "Shirasagi Himegimi", is the public face loved by the people. The Traveler first meets Ayaka here, and Thoma, her attendant, is nearly always at hand.

The Yashiro Commission is regarded as the least controversial of the three Commissions, since its duties are civic and ceremonial rather than military or financial.

Geography: The headquarters is inside the main building of the Kamisato Estate and is marked on the map with the Estate's own icon. It is an enterable interior. A bookcase in the left-hand room holds volumes of A Legend of Sword (Vol. V), New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune (Vol. III) and Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation (Vol. V).

People: Kamisato Ayato is the Commissioner; Ayaka, the Commission's public figure, lives in the Estate; Thoma serves as her attendant and a member of staff. The wiki also lists the Commission's representatives Hirano, Hirotatsu, Madarame Hyakubei, Takami, Furusawa, Kazumasa and Ogawa. Soldiers of the Shogun's Army assigned to the Commission are relaxed compared with those at the Kanjou and Tenryou Commissions.

Governance: The Yashiro Commission is one of three Commissions under the Raiden Shogun, with the Kanjou (finances, borders) and Tenryou (security, military) Commissions. It manages shrines, festivals and cultural events, so it has less influence than those two on paper. All three share equal authority and can check each other. A map text on the Estate says its duties are so pervasive that even Shogunate officials cannot make sense of them.

Culture: Receiving guests is ritualised. Ayaka first receives the Traveler from behind a screen, which Thoma calls a time-honoured tradition within the Yashiro Commission. She puts the screen aside only for those she considers friends.

History: In Three Wishes (Chapter II Act I, 2.0) Thoma brings the Traveler to the Estate, where Ayaka, behind the screen, asks for help against the Vision Hunt Decree and offers an introduction to the Raiden Shogun on one condition: that the Traveler fulfil three small wishes for people who lost their Visions. In A Flower Blooms in a Prison, the Traveler returns to the headquarters, Ayaka steps from behind the screen, declares the Traveler a friend, and dispenses with the screen for Thoma too.

Quests: Appears in Three Wishes and A Flower Blooms in a Prison (Chapter II Act I), in New Shoots from Old Branches (2.6), and in the 5.7 anecdote "Kamisato Ayato: Business".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the headquarters remains the Yashiro Commission's seat. Ayato and Ayaka are its leading figures, Thoma serves there, and the Commission has the most public goodwill of the three. No content from 5.x to 7.1 changes it.

218.comment: Yashiro Commission Headquarters: Ayaka and the screen
218.content: Ayaka meets visitors behind a screen as the Yashiro Commission's daughter, so the public sees her only through her reputation as Shirasagi Himegimi. The Traveler's help with the three Visionless people persuades her to appear in person. Thoma, whose friendship with Ayaka predates his post as attendant, notes that she dispenses with the screen for him and for those she calls friends. When she steps forward she is warm, a little amused by Paimon, and surprisingly different from her formal manner behind it.
